## Start Your OPC Registration

Register your One Person Company (OPC) in India with MCA filing, name approval, PAN, and Certificate of Incorporation to build a compliant, single-owner business.

- MCA Name Approval
- OPC Incorporation
- MOA & AOA Drafting
- PAN & TAN Registration

# One Person Company Registration Online India

One Person Company registration in India allows a single entrepreneur to establish a legally recognized business entity with limited liability protection. The process involves submitting documents to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs through their MCA portal. Registration takes approximately 15 to 20 working days from submission. OPC provides legal recognition and credibility while maintaining simplicity in compliance requirements. This [complete OPC guide for entrepreneurs](https://www.indiafilings.com/one-person-company/one-person-company-a-complete-guide-for-entrepreneurs) covers the complete step-by-step process with all necessary documentation and fees involved.

## What is One Person Company?

Understanding the OPC structure helps entrepreneurs determine whether this business structure suits their ownership requirements, liability protection needs, compliance preferences, and long-term business objectives before starting the incorporation process. You can also learn more about [understanding the One Person Company structure](https://www.indiafilings.com/one-person-company/understanding-one-person-company-structure) before proceeding with registration.

A One Person Company is a corporate structure that permits a single individual to incorporate a company under the Companies Act 2013. This structure combines the benefits of sole proprietorship with corporate liability protection. OPC requires one director, one shareholder, and one nominee. It provides limited liability to the owner while maintaining minimal compliance burden. Entrepreneurs can establish OPC easily with straightforward registration procedures. For a detailed legal overview, refer to [One Person Company under the Companies Act 2013](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/one-person-company-in-india-under-companies-act-2013).

## Who Can Start an OPC Company in India?

Understanding eligibility requirements before incorporation helps entrepreneurs determine whether they qualify for OPC registration and prepare the required identity, residency, ownership, nominee, and incorporation documents. You can review the complete [OPC eligibility requirements](https://www.indiafilings.com/one-person-company/eligibility) before beginning the registration process.

### **Indian Citizens**

Any Indian citizen aged 18 years or above can start an OPC company. They must possess a valid PAN card and Aadhaar number. Indian residents are eligible to incorporate OPC. Solo entrepreneurs and business professionals can establish OPC easily. Citizenship requirements are minimal for registration.

### **Professionals**

Doctors, consultants, and freelancers can register as OPC. Professionals benefit from corporate status and liability protection. Business consultants prefer OPC for credibility. Freelancers gain formal business recognition through OPC. Professional services become legitimate with OPC registration.

### **Entrepreneurs**

Startup founders and solo entrepreneurs can establish OPC. Young business owners prefer OPC for simplicity. Entrepreneurs seek OPC for limited liability protection. Business starters benefit from easier compliance procedures. OPC suits new business ventures and solo operations. Entrepreneurs can also explore [startup registration options](https://www.indiafilings.com/startup) when evaluating different structures for a new business.

### **NRI Individuals**

Non-Resident Indians can register OPC in India. NRI entrepreneurs establish OPC for business operations. Overseas citizens incorporate OPC for Indian investments. NRI status doesn't restrict OPC registration eligibility. Foreign residents can own OPC companies.

## What Documents Are Required for OPC Registration?

OPC registration requires identity proof, address proof, director details, and nominee information. Essential documents include PAN card, Aadhaar, passport, and bank statements. Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association are mandatory. Affidavit of nominee consent is required for registration. Complete documentation ensures smooth and quick approval process. Review the [documents required for OPC registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/one-person-company/document-required) to prepare the necessary paperwork.

| Document Required | Purpose | Format |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PAN Card | Identity and taxation purposes | Digital Copy |
| Aadhaar Card | Verification and address proof | Digital Copy |
| Address Proof | Registered office location | Utility Bill |
| Bank Statement | Financial verification | 3 Months Statement |
| MOA and AOA | Company governing documents | Signed PDF |

## How to Register an One Person Company in India?

OPC registration in India involves seven simple steps through the MCA portal. Start by checking name availability and applying for name approval. Submit all required documents with application forms. Pay registration fees through online payment gateway. Receive OPC registration certificate within 15 to 20 days. Process requires DSC and DIN for director. Complete registration enables immediate business operations and compliance. Follow the detailed [guide on how to register a One Person Company](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/how-to-register-a-one-person-company-opc) for additional information.

### **Step by Step Registration Process**

1. Check Name Availability: Visit MCA portal and check company name availability for your OPC.
2. Apply for Name Approval: Submit name approval application with three name choices through MCA portal online.
3. Get Name Approval: Receive name approval certificate from MCA within 2 to 5 working days after submission.
4. Prepare Documents: Gather all required documents including [PAN](https://www.indiafilings.com/pan-card), Aadhaar, address proof, and bank statements.
5. Submit Registration Application: File complete application with MOA, AOA, and all documents on MCA portal.
6. Pay Registration Fees: Complete payment of applicable registration fees through online mode.
7. Receive Certificate: Get OPC registration certificate and CIN number from [MCA portal](https://www.indiafilings.com/mca-services) after approval.

## How to Choose a Company Name for OPC Registration?

Choosing an appropriate company name is important for establishing a recognizable identity while meeting naming requirements and ensuring that the proposed name can be approved during incorporation. Before finalizing a name, entrepreneurs should [check company name availability](https://www.indiafilings.com/check-company-name-availability) to avoid conflicts or rejection.

### **Unique and Memorable**

Choose distinctive names that reflect your business nature and values. Memorable names help customer recall and brand recognition. Avoid generic terms that are too common or confusing. Unique names differentiate your OPC from competitors effectively. Strong naming creates lasting business identity and credibility.

### **Follow MCA Guidelines**

Names must comply with MCA naming rules and regulations. Avoid restricted words and prohibited terminology in naming. Company name should indicate business activity or type. Check MCA guidelines before finalizing your OPC name. Compliance ensures smooth name approval from authorities. Entrepreneurs can review the [OPC name approval process](https://www.indiafilings.com/one-person-company/name-approval) for additional guidance.

### **Easy to Remember**

Simple names are easier for customers to recall and pronounce. Short company names attract better brand recognition and recall. Avoid complex spellings that confuse potential customers. Easy names facilitate better marketing and business growth. Simplicity improves customer communication and brand loyalty.

### **Domain Availability**

Ensure matching domain name is available online for registration. Website domain should align with company name for consistency. Online presence strengthens business branding and digital visibility. Domain names enhance professional online image and credibility. Matching domain and company name creates cohesive brand identity. You can also review [OPC name availability](https://www.indiafilings.com/one-person-company/name-availability) information before selecting your preferred business name.

## How Much Does OPC Registration Cost in India?

OPC registration fees in India vary based on authorized capital and business nature. Government filing fees range from 500 to 5000 rupees. Professional consultation and documentation charges add to total cost. Total registration expense typically ranges from 5000 to 15000 rupees. Investment depends on whether you hire professional assistance or self-register. For a detailed breakdown, review the [OPC registration fee guide](https://www.indiafilings.com/one-person-company/opc-registration-fee-how-to-apply-easily).

| Service Component | Cost Range | Remarks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name Approval | ₹500 - ₹1,000 | MCA filing charges |
| Registration Filing | ₹1,000 - ₹2,000 | Government fees |
| Professional Help | ₹2,000 - ₹5,000 | Optional service charge |
| [DSC](https://www.indiafilings.com/digital-signature) and DIN | ₹2,000 - ₹3,000 | Digital signature certificate |
| Total Cost | ₹5,000 - ₹15,000 | Approximate total investment |

View the detailed [OPC registration pricing](https://www.indiafilings.com/one-person-company/pricing) and cost breakdown for your business requirements today.

## How Long Does OPC Registration Take?

OPC registration timelines depend on name approval, document preparation, application filing, MCA processing, and whether additional clarification or resubmission is required. Understanding the expected timeline helps entrepreneurs plan their incorporation and business launch effectively. The [OPC registration process](https://www.indiafilings.com/one-person-company/one-person-company-registration-process) provides further information about the stages involved.

| Registration Stage | Time Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name Availability Check | 1 - 2 Days | Instant online availability verification |
| Name Approval | 2 - 5 Days | MCA approval of company name |
| Document Preparation | 3 - 5 Days | [MOA](https://www.indiafilings.com/memorandum-of-association-amendment), [AOA](https://www.indiafilings.com/aoa-amendment), and affidavits preparation |
| Application Submission | 1 Day | Filing application on MCA portal |
| MCA Processing | 5 - 10 Days | MCA review and verification of documents |
| Certificate Issuance | 1 - 2 Days | Registration certificate download from portal |
| Total Time | 15 - 25 Days | Complete registration timeline |

## What Are the Benefits of a One Person Company?

An OPC can offer several advantages to solo entrepreneurs, particularly those seeking limited liability, formal business recognition, simplified management, and a comparatively lower compliance burden. Entrepreneurs can explore the [benefits of One Person Company](https://www.indiafilings.com/one-person-company/what-is-one-person-company-opc-learn-benefit) to understand these advantages in greater detail.

### **Limited Liability Protection**

OPC provides limited liability to the owner for business debts. Personal assets remain protected from business liabilities and creditors. Owner's personal wealth is separate from company obligations. Liability limitation ensures financial security and risk management. Protection encourages business growth with reduced personal risk exposure.

### **Easy Registration Process**

OPC registration is simpler compared to other company structures. Minimal documentation and fewer compliance requirements simplify establishment. Quick approval from MCA within 15 to 25 days. Online registration process is convenient and user-friendly. Simplified procedures reduce registration complexity and time investment.

### **Professional Credibility**

OPC status enhances business credibility and professional image. Corporate structure attracts better customers and business partners. Professional recognition improves market positioning and brand value. Clients prefer working with registered company entities. Credibility facilitates business growth and partnership opportunities.

### **Lower Compliance Burden**

OPC has minimal compliance requirements compared to private limited. Annual filing requirements are simpler and less documentation intensive. Board meetings and resolutions are not mandatory for OPC. Compliance costs are significantly lower for OPC companies. Reduced compliance burden allows focus on business operations. Discover the [seven reasons to incorporate a One Person Company](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/indiafilings-et-wealth-7-reasons-to-incorporate-one-person-company) for your entrepreneurial success.

## What Is the OPC Registration Number?

The OPC registration number is called CIN or Corporate Identification Number. CIN is a 21-character alphanumeric code assigned by MCA. Registration number appears on all official company documents and certificates. CIN serves as unique identifier for your OPC company. Number is generated automatically upon successful registration approval.

## What Compliance Is Required for an OPC?

Ongoing compliance is essential after incorporation to maintain the company's legal status, meet statutory obligations, keep accurate records, and avoid additional fees, notices, or penalties. Owners should understand the [OPC annual filing requirements](https://www.indiafilings.com/one-person-company/understanding-opc-annual-filing-requirements) before beginning business operations.

### **Annual Filing Requirements**

OPC must file annual financial statements and balance sheet. Income statement and cash flow statement are mandatory filings. Annual reports must be submitted to MCA portal. Auditor certification may be required based on turnover. Timely filing ensures regulatory compliance and business legitimacy.

### **Tax Compliance**

OPC must file income tax returns annually with tax authorities. GST registration and filing are mandatory if applicable. Tax payments must be made on time to avoid penalties. Professional tax consultation ensures accurate compliance procedures. Tax filing demonstrates financial responsibility and regulatory adherence.

### **Statutory Filings**

Register with appropriate statutory authorities and regulatory bodies. Employee provident fund registration is needed if having employees. Professional licenses and permits must be obtained as required. Regular compliance updates must be submitted to authorities. Statutory adherence prevents legal issues and penalties.

### **Record Maintenance**

Maintain detailed books of accounts and financial records. Store all business documents and receipts for seven years. Register should document all transactions and meetings. Financial records must be available for audit purposes. Proper documentation ensures transparency and regulatory compliance.

## What Are the Compliance Due Dates for an OPC in India?

OPC compliance due dates are fixed by MCA and government authorities. Annual financial statements must be filed within 30 days. Income tax returns are due by July 31st each year. GST filing deadlines vary based on business turnover. Adhering to due dates prevents penalties and legal issues. The [OPC annual filing and ROC compliance guide](https://www.indiafilings.com/one-person-company/opc-annual-filing-roc-compliance-guide) can help businesses understand ongoing filing requirements.

| Compliance Type | Due Date | Frequency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Annual Financial Statements | Within 30 Days of Fiscal Year End | Annually |
| Income Tax Return Filing | July 31st of Each Year | Annually |
| GST Filing | Monthly or Quarterly Based on Turnover | Monthly or Quarterly |
| Balance Sheet Filing | Within 30 Days of AGM | Annually |
| Statutory Compliance Reports | As Per Regulatory Requirements | Quarterly or Annually |

## What OPC Compliances Are Required to Avoid Penalties?

OPC must maintain strict compliance to avoid government penalties and fines. Delayed filing attracts penalty charges from MCA and tax authorities. Regular compliance updates prevent legal notices and regulatory actions. Proper documentation protects business from penalties and suspension. Timely compliance ensures smooth operations without legal complications.

## What Is the Checklist for OPC Registration Online?

A comprehensive checklist ensures smooth OPC registration without delays. Before starting registration, arrange all required documents and information. Verify company name availability and apply for name approval. Collect identity documents, address proofs, and financial statements. Prepare MOA and AOA documents with proper signatures. Complete the OPC registration process systematically and efficiently. Entrepreneurs can also follow a [step-by-step OPC registration guide](https://www.indiafilings.com/one-person-company/register-an-opc-stepbystep-guide) when preparing their application.

### **OPC Registration Checklist**

- Verify company name availability on MCA portal
- Collect PAN card and Aadhaar details
- Gather address proof documents for office location
- Arrange bank statements for last three months
- Prepare Memorandum of Association document
- Draft Articles of Association for company
- Get digital signature certificate for director
- Obtain nominee affidavit and consent form
- Prepare director identification number application
- Arrange proof of business or residential address
- Collect identity proof for director
- Prepare passport size photographs if required
- Organize all document scans in digital format
- Review all documents for completeness
- Keep payment details ready for registration
- Submit all documents on MCA portal
- Monitor application status regularly
- Follow up with MCA for any clarifications

## What Is the Difference Between OPC, Private Limited Company, and LLP?

OPC, Private Limited, and LLP are different business structures with distinct features. OPC has single owner while Private Limited requires minimum two directors. LLP is partnership structure with shared ownership and management. Each structure has different compliance requirements and taxation benefits. Choosing right structure depends on business needs and growth plans. You can compare the [differences between OPC and Private Limited Company](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/one-person-company-vs-private-limited-company) before making a decision.

| Feature | One Person Company | Private Limited Company | Limited Liability Partnership |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ownership | Single Individual | Minimum Two Shareholders | Two or More Partners |
| Directors Required | One Director Required | Minimum Two Directors | One Designated Partner |
| Liability | Limited to Capital | Limited to Capital | Limited to Capital |
| Compliance Burden | Minimal Compliance | Significant Compliance | Moderate Compliance |
| Registration Cost | ₹5,000 to ₹15,000 | ₹10,000 to ₹25,000 | ₹8,000 to ₹20,000 |
| Board Meetings | Not Mandatory | Quarterly Meetings Required | Annual Meeting Required |

LLP can be another option for businesses with multiple owners, so entrepreneurs can also explore [LLP registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/llp-registration) when comparing business structures.

## Frequently asked questions

Common questions aboutOne Person Company Registration in India for Solo Entrepreneurs.

What is an OPC, and how does it differ from other business structures?

An OPC, or One Person Company, is a unique business structure in India that allows a single individual to operate as a company, combining the advantages of a sole proprietorship with the legal protection of a private limited company.

When was the concept of OPC introduced in India?

The concept of OPC was introduced under the Companies Act of 2013.

What is the primary objective of OPC registration?

The primary objective of OPC registration is to promote entrepreneurship and encourage the formalization of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs).

What are the eligibility criteria for OPC registration?

To register an OPC, you must be a natural person and an Indian citizen, resident in India for at least 182 days during the previous calendar year. The OPC must have a minimum authorized capital of Rs 1,00,000, and a nominee must be appointed.

Can an OPC engage in financial activities like banking or insurance?

No, an OPC cannot engage in financial activities like banking, insurance, or investments.

What happens if the OPCs paid-up share capital exceeds 50 lakhs or its annual turnover exceeds 2 Crores?

In such cases, the OPC must be converted into a private limited company to comply with regulatory requirements.

How many OPCs can an individual establish?

An individual can establish only one OPC.

Can an OPC have a minor as its member?

No, an OPC cannot have a minor as its member.

What are the advantages of registering an OPC?

Advantages include limited liability, easy fundraising, reduced compliance, simple incorporation, efficient management, and perpetual succession.

Are there any disadvantages to registering an OPC?

Yes, disadvantages include suitability primarily for small businesses, restrictions on certain activities, and a potential lack of clear distinction between ownership and management.

What is the registration process for an OPC in India?

OPC registration is done through the SPICe+ form, involving obtaining a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC), Director Identification Number (DIN), name reservation, preparation of MOA and AOA, filing forms, and obtaining a Certificate of Incorporation.

What documents are required for OPC registration?

Required documents include MOA, AOA, nominees consent, proof of registered office, declarations, and a compliance certificate.

What is the significance of obtaining a Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)?

A DSC is used for electronically signing documents during the registration process.

What is a Director Identification Number (DIN), and why is it required?

A DIN is a unique identification number for directors, and its required for legal compliance and governance.

How is the registered office address determined for an OPC?

The registered office address should be decided and declared during the registration process.

What is the role of a nominee in an OPC?

A nominee is appointed to take over the OPC in the event of the directors death or incapacity.

What is the Certificate of Incorporation, and when is it issued?

The Certificate of Incorporation is an official document issued by the ROC after approval, signifying the successful registration of an OPC.

Why should I choose IndiaFilings for OPC registration?

IndiaFilings offers expert guidance, simplifies the registration process, ensures compliance, and provides dedicated support to make OPC registration hassle-free.

What are the post-incorporation formalities for an OPC?

Post-incorporation formalities may include filing a notice regarding the registered office within 30 days after incorporation.

How can IndiaFilings assist with post-incorporation formalities for OPCs?

IndiaFilings experts are ready to assist in fulfilling OPC compliance requirements, ensuring your business remains in full legal compliance.

# Partnership Firm Registration in India

A **partnership firm** is one of the most preferred business structures in India, where two or more individuals come together to run a business and share profits and losses. Governed by the **Indian Partnership Act, 1932**, a partnership firm offers flexibility, shared responsibility, and ease of formation. Whether you are starting a new venture or formalizing an existing business, understanding the complete **[partnership firm registration process](https://www.indiafilings.com/partnership/partnership-firm-registration-guide)** is the first step towards building a legally recognized and credible business in India.

## What is Partnership Firm Registration in India?

**Partnership firm registration in India** is the process of legally registering a business entity formed by two or more individuals under the **Indian Partnership Act, 1932**. Although registration is not mandatory, a **registered partnership firm** enjoys several legal benefits over an unregistered one, including the right to file suits in court and claim set-offs.

The registration is done with the **Registrar of Firms** of the respective state government. A **partnership deed** is the foundation of every partnership firm, outlining the rights, duties, and profit-sharing ratio of each partner.

### Legal Framework – Indian Partnership Act 1932

The **Indian Partnership Act, 1932** governs all aspects of **partnership firm registration** in India. It defines the rights and liabilities of partners, rules for dissolution, and provisions for registration. The Act provides the complete legal framework for **[partnership business setup](https://www.indiafilings.com/startup)** in the country.

## What are the Types of Partnership Firms in India?

Understanding the different types of **partnership firm registration** helps you choose the right structure for your **two person business india** or multi-partner venture. There are five major types of **partnership business setup** recognized in India:

### General Partnership (GP)

A **General Partnership (GP)** is the most common and simplest form of **[partnership firm](https://www.indiafilings.com/partnership)** [in India](https://www.indiafilings.com/partnership). In this type, all partners share equal rights and responsibilities in managing the business and are jointly and severally liable for the debts and obligations of the firm.

- All partners have **unlimited liability**
- Every partner has the right to participate in the management of the business
- Profits and losses are shared as per the **[partnership deed](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/partnership-deed-format)**
- Governed by the **Indian Partnership Act, 1932**
- Ideal for small businesses, traders, and professional service firms

### Limited Liability Partnership (LLP)

A **[Limited Liability Partnership](https://www.indiafilings.com/llp-registration) (LLP)** is a hybrid business structure that combines the features of a **general partnership** and a company. It is governed by the **Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008** and is one of the most preferred structures for professionals and startups in India.

- Partners enjoy **limited liability** protection up to their capital contribution
- LLP is a **separate legal entity** distinct from its partners
- Mandatory registration with the **[Ministry of Corporate Affairs](https://www.indiafilings.com/mca-services) (MCA)**
- No maximum limit on the number of partners
- Lower compliance burden compared to a Private Limited Company

| Feature | General Partnership | Limited Liability Partnership (LLP) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Liability | Unlimited | Limited |
| Legal Entity | No | Yes |
| Registration | Optional | Mandatory |
| Governing Law | Indian Partnership Act, 1932 | LLP Act, 2008 |
| Suitable For | Small Businesses | Professionals & Startups |

### Partnership at Will

A **Partnership at Will** is a type of **partnership firm** where there is no fixed duration or specific end date mentioned in the **partnership deed**. The partnership continues as long as all partners are willing to continue and can be dissolved at any time by any partner by giving notice to the other partners.

- No fixed term or duration for the partnership
- Any partner can dissolve the firm by giving a **written notice** to other partners
- Most flexible form of **partnership business setup** in India
- Governed under **Section 7 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932**
- Commonly used by small traders and family-run businesses

### Particular Partnership (Partnership for a Specific Venture)

A **Particular Partnership** is formed for a specific project, venture, or purpose. Once the objective of the partnership is achieved or the specific venture is completed, the partnership automatically dissolves. This is ideal for businesses that collaborate for a one-time project or a fixed-term goal.

- Formed for a **specific purpose or project**
- Automatically dissolves upon completion of the venture
- Partners share profits and losses only for that specific venture
- Governed under **Section 8 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932**
- Suitable for **construction projects, joint ventures**, and event-based businesses

### Limited Partnership (LP)

A **Limited Partnership (LP)** consists of two types of partners — **General Partners** who manage the business and have unlimited liability, and **[Limited Partners](https://www.indiafilings.com/public-limited-company)** who invest capital but have limited liability up to their capital contribution. Limited Partners do not participate in the day-to-day management of the firm.

- Comprises both **general partners** and **limited partners**
- Limited partners enjoy **liability protection** up to their investment
- General partners have **unlimited liability** and manage the business
- Limited partners cannot participate in the **management of the firm**
- Commonly used in **investment funds, real estate, and private equity** ventures

| Type of Partnership | Liability | Duration | Management | Best Suited For |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **General Partnership (GP)** | Unlimited | Ongoing | All Partners | Small Businesses |
| **Limited Liability Partnership (LLP)** | Limited | Ongoing | Designated Partners | Professionals & Startups |
| **Partnership at Will** | Unlimited | No Fixed Term | All Partners | Flexible Small Businesses |
| **Particular Partnership** | Unlimited | Project-Based | All Partners | Joint Ventures & Projects |
| **Limited Partnership (LP)** | Mixed | Ongoing | General Partners Only | Investment & Real Estate |

## What is the Difference Between Registered and Unregistered Partnership Firm in India?

One of the most common questions during the **partnership firm registration process** is understanding the key differences between a registered and unregistered firm:

| Feature | Registered Partnership Firm | Unregistered Partnership Firm |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Legal Recognition | Yes | Limited |
| Can File Lawsuit | Yes | No |
| Bank Loan Eligibility | Easy | Difficult |
| Government Tenders | Eligible | Not Eligible |
| Claim Set-offs | Allowed | Not Allowed |
| Credibility | High | Low |

## Who Should Opt for a Partnership Firm in India?

A **partnership firm** is an ideal business structure for the following types of entrepreneurs and professionals. If you are unsure about the right business structure, exploring [**startup registration**](https://www.indiafilings.com/startup) options can help you make the best decision for your business goals.

### Ideal Candidates for Partnership Firm in India

- Small and medium-sized businesses looking for a **partnership business setup** with minimal compliance
- Family-owned businesses where members want to pool resources
- Professional service firms such as lawyers, chartered accountants, and doctors
- Trading and retail businesses with **two person business india** model
- Startups in the early stage who want a flexible structure before graduating to an LLP or Private Limited Company

### When to Avoid a Partnership Firm in India

- When partners want **limited liability** protection – consider LLP instead
- When the business plans to raise external funding or venture capital
- When the business involves high-risk activities with significant financial exposure

## How to Choose a Partnership Firm Name in India?

Choosing the right name is a critical step in **partnership firm name registration**. Here are the key guidelines to follow:

### Rules for Partnership Firm Name in India

- The name must not be identical or similar to any existing registered firm
- The name must not include words like **Emperor, Crown, Empire, or Royal** without prior approval
- Avoid using words that suggest government affiliation
- The name must not violate the **Emblems and Names (Prevention of Improper Use) Act, 1950**
- The name should reflect the nature of the **[business partnership india](https://www.indiafilings.com/)**

### Tips for Choosing the Right Name in India

- Keep it short, simple, and easy to remember
- Ensure the domain name is available for online presence
- Check [trademark availability](https://www.indiafilings.com/trademark/search) before finalizing the name
- Include the partners' surnames for a professional appeal

## What is the Eligibility for Partnership Firm Registration in India?

Before proceeding with the **partnership firm registration process**, it is important to understand the eligibility conditions:

### Eligibility of Partners in India

- Minimum **2 partners** are required to form a partnership firm
- Maximum **50 partners** are allowed as per the Companies Act, 2013
- Partners must be Indian citizens or NRIs (with restrictions)
- Partners must be of sound mind and not insolvent
- Minors cannot be a full partner but can be admitted to the benefits of the firm

### Restrictions on Eligibility in India

- A person already declared insolvent cannot be a partner
- Certain regulated professions may have specific restrictions
- Foreign nationals require prior RBI approval for certain business activities

## What is the Checklist Required for Partnership Firm Registration in India?

Having the right documents ready ensures a smooth **partnership firm registration online** process. Below is the complete checklist:

### Identity Proof Documents in India

- [PAN Card](https://www.indiafilings.com/pan-card) of all partners
- Aadhaar Card / Voter ID / Passport of all partners
- Passport-size photographs of all partners

### Address Proof Documents in India

- Electricity bill / Water bill of the business address
- Rent agreement (if the premises is rented)
- NOC from the property owner

### Partnership Deed Requirements in India

- **Partnership deed** drafted on stamp paper of requisite value
- Duly signed by all partners
- Notarized copy of the partnership deed
- **Partnership firm name registration** details included in the deed

## What is a Partnership Deed and Why is it Important in India?

A **partnership deed** is the most critical document in a **partnership firm registration**. It is a legal agreement between the partners that outlines all the terms and conditions of the partnership.

### Key Clauses in Partnership Deed in India

- Name and address of the firm and all partners
- Nature and scope of the business
- Capital contribution by each partner
- Profit and loss sharing ratio
- Rights, duties, and obligations of each partner
- Rules for admission, retirement, or death of a partner
- Process for **partnership firm dissolution**

### Notarization & Stamp Duty in India

The **partnership deed registration** must be executed on non-judicial stamp paper. The stamp duty varies from state to state. For example, in Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra, the stamp duty ranges from ₹200 to ₹500 depending on the capital contribution.

## What is the Partnership Firm Registration Process in India?

The **partnership firm registration process** in India involves submitting an application to the [Registrar of Firms](https://www.indiafilings.com/partnership/effects-of-non-registration-of-a-partnership-firm) along with the required documents and fees. The process can be completed both online and offline depending on the state.

### Online Partnership Registration Process in India

- Visit the official website of the respective state's Registrar of Firms
- Fill in the **[online partnership registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/partnership/register-your-partnership-firm-easily)** application form

### Offline Partnership Registration Process in India

- Submit Form 1 along with all required documents

## What is the Step-by-Step Process of Partnership Firm Registration in India?

Follow this simple step-by-step guide for **[how to register partnership firm](https://www.indiafilings.com/partnership/partnership-firm-registration-process-stepbystep-guide)** in India:

1. **Step 1 – Draft the Partnership Deed:** Prepare a comprehensive **partnership deed registration** document that includes business name, nature of business, profit-sharing ratio, capital contribution, and rights & duties of each partner.
2. **Step 2 – Notarize the Deed:** Get the **partners agreement** notarized on stamp paper of appropriate value as per your state's Stamp Act.
3. **Step 3 – Apply to the Registrar of Firms:** Submit Form 1 (Application for Registration) along with all required documents to the **Registrar of Firms** of your state.
4. **Step 4 – Pay the Registration Fee:** Pay the applicable **partnership firm registration fee** to the Registrar of Firms.
5. **Step 5 – Obtain Registration Certificate:** Once verified, the Registrar will issue a **partnership registration certificate**, officially registering your firm.
6. **Step 6 – Apply for PAN & GST:** Apply for a **partnership firm PAN card** and **GST registration for partnership** if applicable.

## What is the Registration Certificate for a Partnership Firm in India?

A **partnership registration certificate** is an official document issued by the Registrar of Firms confirming that the firm is legally registered under the **Indian Partnership Act, 1932**.

## Frequently asked questions

Common questions aboutPartnership Firm Registration Online in India.

What is the registration of a partnership?

Registration of partnership in India is legally formalizing a partnership firm by filing an application with the Registrar of Firms under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932. The registration process involves providing details about the partnership firm, such as its name, location, partners' details, and the terms and conditions of the partnership agreement.

Is it compulsory to register a partnership?

Registration of a partner to a partnership firm is not compulsory in India. However, if a new partner joins the partnership firm, the partnership deed should be amended, and a supplementary agreement should be executed. While registration of partners is not required, the partnership firm must be registered with the Registrar of Firms under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932.

Who is eligible for partnership?

Under the Indian Partnership Act, the following Individual/entities are eligible to become partners in a partnership firm:

- **Individual:** Any person who is of sound mind, not a minor, not an undercharged insolvent, and not disqualified from entering into a contract by law can become a partner in a partnership firm.
- **Firm:** A registered partnership firm can become a partner in another partnership firm.
- **Hindu Undivided Family (HUF):** The Karta of a HUF can become a partner in a partnership firm in his capacity if he has contributed his self-acquired or personal skill and labor to the partnership firm.
- **Company:** Companies are juristic persons and can become partners in a partnership firm if their objects permit it.
- **Trustees:** Trustees of private religious trusts, family trusts, and Hindu mutts can enter into partnerships unless their constitutions or objects forbid it.

How much capital is required to start a Partnership?

A Partnership firm can be started with any amount of capital. There is no minimum requirement as such.

What are the advantages of registering a Partnership firm?

It is very advisable to register a Partnership firm as a Registered Partnership Firm can file a suit in any court against any of the Partners or firm for the enforcement of any right arising from the contract referred by the Partnership Act.

Also, only a Registered Partnership Firm can claim set-off or other proceedings in a dispute with a party.

Is a partnership firm a separate legal entity?

The Partnership firm and the partners are the same in the eyes of the law. In Partnership firms, the liability of the Partners is also unlimited and all the Partners are said to be jointly and severally liable for the liabilities of the firm. Hence, No Partnership firm doesn't have separate legal existence of its own.

Is it compulsory for partnership firms to file income tax returns?

A Partnership Firm must file the returns of Income irrespective of the number of profits or losses made by the Partners.

Can a person transfer to a partnership firm?

There are restrictions on the Transfer of ownership interest in a Partnership Firm. A Partner cannot transfer his or her interest in the firm to any person without the consent of all other partners.

What is a Partnership deed?

A Partnership deed is an agreement between the Partner that highlights the terms and the rules of the Partnership among the Partners. Ensure that two or more individuals as partner to agree on firm name to register partnership deed.

Why is a Partnership deed necessary?

The Partnership deed lays down all the Terms and Conditions of the Partnerships. As it regulates the rights and duties of each partner. A Partnership deed is a very crucial document. Hence, it is essential to register partnership deed.

How can I transfer to my partnership firm?

There are restrictions on the transfer of the Partnership Firm. A Partner cannot transfer his / her interest in the firm to anyone without the consent of all other partners.

Is audit required for a Partnership?

In the case of Partnerships, it is not necessary to prepare audited financial statements each year. However, a tax audit may be necessary based on turnover and other criteria.

Can I convert my Partnership firm into a Company/ LLP?

Yes, there's a specified procedure for converting a Partnership firm into a Company or LLP. However, the procedure is very cumbersome and time-consuming. It will be wise if an entrepreneur considers starting an LLP or a Company instead of a Partnership firm.

How to open a bank account for a Partnership firm?

To open a bank account for a Partnership firm a registered Partnership deed along with an identity proof and address proof of the Partner is to be provided.

How will IndiaFilings help you in Partnership firm registration?

An associate from IndiaFilings will understand your business requirements and help you start a Partnership firm by drafting the Partnership deed.

Based on the requirement we also help the partnership firms to become Registered Partnership Firms.

How many people are required to start a Partnership firm?

In a Partnership firm, a minimum of 2 members are required and a maximum of 20 partners are allowed.

Who can be a Partner in a Partnership firm?

An individual who is an Indian citizen and a resident of India can partner in a Partnership firm. Nonresident Indians and Individuals belonging to Indian Origin can invest in a Partnership only with the approval of the Government.

What documents are required to register a Partnership firm?

For the partners, it is necessary to submit a PAN card along with the identity and address proof. It is recommended to draft a Partnership Deed which is to be signed by all the Partners.

MOA contains company's objectives and powers for conducting business. AOA specifies rules for directors, shareholders, and meetings. Both documents must comply with Companies Act requirements. ## Frequently asked questions

Common questions aboutCompany Registration Online in India.

What is a Company Registration?

Company Registration is the legal process of incorporating a business entity under the Companies Act, 2013, governed by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. It gives the business a separate legal identity, limited liability protection, and the ability to enter contracts, own assets, and raise funds in its own name.

How many types of company registration are there?

There are several types of company registration in India:

- Private Limited Company
- Public Limited Company
- One Person Company (OPC)
- Limited Liability Partnership (LLP)
- Section 8 Company (Non-Profit)
- Nidhi Company
- Producer Company

Which type of company registration is best for a startup?

A Private Limited Company is the most preferred choice for startups. It offers limited liability protection, easy fundraising options, separate legal identity, and credibility with investors. It is also eligible for various startup benefits and government schemes under the Startup India initiative.

What is the difference between a Private Limited Company and an LLP?

A Private Limited Company is suitable for businesses seeking investment and growth, while an LLP offers flexibility with fewer compliances. The key differences are:

- Private Limited Company has shareholders and directors; LLP has partners
- Private Limited Company can raise equity funding; LLP cannot
- LLP has lesser annual compliances compared to a Private Limited Company

What is the difference between a Private Limited Company and a Public Limited Company?

A Private Limited Company restricts share transfer and can have a maximum of 200 shareholders, while a Public Limited Company can offer shares to the general public. A Public Limited Company requires a minimum of 7 shareholders and 3 directors, whereas a Private Limited Company requires only 2 shareholders and 2 directors.

What are the main features of a Company Registration?

The main features of a registered company include:

- Separate legal entity from its owners
- Limited liability protection for shareholders
- Perpetual succession
- Ability to own property and enter contracts
- Transferability of shares
- Governed by the Companies Act, 2013

What are the advantages of a Company Registration?

Registering a company offers several advantages such as limited liability protection, separate legal identity, easier access to funding, enhanced credibility, perpetual existence, and tax benefits. It also builds trust with clients, vendors, and investors, making it easier to grow and scale the business.

What are the minimum requirements for a Company Registration?

The minimum requirements for company registration in India are:

- Minimum 2 directors (for Private Limited Company)
- Minimum 2 shareholders
- A unique company name
- A registered office address in India
- Valid identity and address proof of directors and shareholders

How many directors are required for a Company Registration?

A Private Limited Company requires a minimum of 2 directors and can have a maximum of 15 directors. At least one director must be a resident of India, meaning they should have stayed in India for at least 182 days during the previous financial year.

How many shareholders are required for a Company Registration?

A Private Limited Company requires a minimum of 2 shareholders and a maximum of 200 shareholders. A One Person Company (OPC) can be registered with just 1 shareholder. The same person can be both a director and a shareholder in a company.

Can a foreign national register a company in India?

Yes, a foreign national can be a director or shareholder in an Indian company. However, at least one director must be an Indian resident. Foreign nationals must provide a notarized and apostilled copy of their passport, address proof, and other KYC documents for company registration.

How to choose a name for a Company Registration?

When choosing a company name, ensure it is unique, not identical or similar to any existing company or trademark. The name should reflect the business activity and end with Private Limited or LLP as applicable. You can check name availability on the MCA portal before applying. Avoid restricted or prohibited words.

How to check Company Registration name availability?

You can check company name availability through the [IndiaFilings Company Registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-registration) service, which guides you through the MCA portal name search process. Simply enter your preferred name to check if it is available and not already registered or trademarked.

How do I check if a company is registered in India?

You can verify if a company is registered in India by visiting the Ministry of Corporate Affairs portal and searching by company name or CIN number. The MCA database provides details such as company status, date of incorporation, registered address, and director information for all registered companies.

What documents are required for Company Registration?

The documents required for company registration in India are:

- PAN card of all directors and shareholders
- Aadhaar card or Voter ID or Passport
- Latest bank statement or utility bill as address proof
- Passport-size photographs
- Proof of registered office address such as rent agreement or ownership document
- NOC from the property owner

How to register a Company in India?

The steps to register a company in India are:

- Obtain Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) for directors
- Apply for Director Identification Number (DIN)
- Reserve a unique company name through RUN (Reserve Unique Name)
- File SPICe+ form with required documents on MCA portal
- Receive Certificate of Incorporation from the Registrar of Companies

What are the government fees for company registration?

The government fees for company registration depend on the authorized share capital of the company. For companies with a share capital up to Rs. 1 lakh, the fees are nominal. Additional stamp duty charges vary from state to state. Professional charges may apply separately for assistance with documentation and filing.

How long does company registration take in India?

Company registration in India typically takes 7 to 10 working days, subject to document verification and MCA processing time. The timeline may vary depending on the accuracy of documents submitted and the workload at the Registrar of Companies office at the time of filing.

What is a Certificate of Incorporation for a Company Registration?

A Certificate of Incorporation is the official document issued by the Registrar of Companies confirming that a company has been legally registered under the Companies Act, 2013. It contains the Company Identification Number (CIN), date of incorporation, and the company name, and serves as proof of the company's legal existence.

Is a name board mandatory for a Company Registration?

Yes, every registered company in India is required to display its name and registered office address on a name board outside its office premises. The name board must be in English and also in the local language of the state where the registered office is located, as per the Companies Act, 2013.

Can an LLP be converted into a Company Registration?

Yes, an existing LLP can be converted into a Private Limited Company as per the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013. The process involves filing the required forms with the MCA, obtaining approval, and complying with conversion rules. All assets, liabilities, and obligations of the LLP are transferred to the new company.

What are the annual compliances for a Company Registration?

A registered company must fulfill the following annual compliances:

- Filing of Annual Return (MGT-7)
- Filing of Financial Statements (AOC-4)
- Conducting Annual General Meeting (AGM)
- Filing of Income Tax Return
- Maintaining statutory registers and records
- ROC filings within due dates to avoid penalties

# Section 8 Company Registration Online in India

**Section 8 company registration in India** is the legally recognized process of incorporating a non-profit organization under the **Companies Act, 2013**. It is ideal for individuals and organizations aiming to promote education, charity, science, religion, arts, or social welfare. A **Section 8 company** enjoys distinct legal identity, [income tax benefits](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax), and higher credibility compared to other non-profit structures.

## What is Section 8 Company Registration in India?

A **Section 8 company** is a type of non-profit organization registered under **Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013**, governed by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA). It is incorporated with the objective of promoting commerce, art, science, sports, education, research, social welfare, religion, charity, or environmental protection. Unlike other companies, a **Section 8 company** does not distribute profits to its members — all income is applied towards promoting its stated objectives.

### Features of Section 8 Company

- Registered under **Companies Act, 2013**
- Separate legal entity from its members
- No distribution of profits to members
- Limited liability for all members
- No minimum capital requirement
- Higher credibility compared to Trust or Society
- Eligible for **[12A and 80G registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/12a-80g-registration)** for tax exemptions

### Key Differences Between Trust, Society, and a Section 8 Company

Choosing the right non-profit structure is critical. Here is a comparison between [**Trust registration**](https://www.indiafilings.com/trust-registration), [**Society registration**](https://www.indiafilings.com/society-registration), and Section 8 Company:

| Parameter | Trust | Society | Section 8 Company |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Governing Law | Indian Trusts Act, 1882 | Societies Registration Act, 1860 | Companies Act, 2013 |
| Registration Authority | Sub-Registrar | Registrar of Societies | Ministry of Corporate Affairs |
| Minimum Members | 2 Trustees | 7 Members | 2 Directors |
| Legal Status | Not a separate legal entity | Separate legal entity | Separate legal entity |
| Credibility | Moderate | Moderate | High |
| Foreign Funding ( [FCRA](https://www.indiafilings.com/fcra-registration)) | Eligible | Eligible | Eligible |
| [Compliance](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-annual-filing) | Less Stringent | Moderate | More Stringent |

### Section 8 Company vs NGO

Many people confuse Section 8 companies with NGOs. Learn more about the [**difference between Section 8 company and NGO**](https://www.indiafilings.com/section-8-company-registration/difference-between-section-8-company-ngo) to make a well-informed decision about your non-profit registration.

### Section 8 Company vs Private Limited Company

A **Section 8 company** differs from a regular [**company registration in India**](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-registration) in that it cannot distribute profits to its shareholders. All surplus income must be reinvested towards the company's charitable objectives as stated in its Memorandum of Association.

## Why Should You Register a Section 8 Company in India?

Registering a **Section 8 company in India** offers significant legal, financial, and reputational advantages for non-profit initiatives. Here are the top reasons why you should consider this structure for your **[nonprofit company registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/section-8-company-registration)**:

### Key Benefits of Section 8 Company Registration

- **Tax Exemptions:** Eligible for [income tax](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax) exemption under Sections 12A and 80G of the Income Tax Act.
- **[Limited Liability](https://www.indiafilings.com/llp-registration):** Members' personal assets are protected from company liabilities.
- **Separate Legal Entity:** Can own property, sue, and be sued in its own name.
- **Higher Credibility:** Regulated by [MCA](https://www.indiafilings.com/mca-services), making it more credible to donors and government bodies.
- **No Minimum Capital:** No mandatory minimum paid-up capital requirement.
- **Perpetual Succession:** Continues to exist regardless of changes in membership.
- **Foreign Funding Eligible:** Can receive foreign contributions under [FCRA](https://www.indiafilings.com/fcra-registration) after registration.
- **Stamp Duty Exemption:** Exempted from stamp duty on registration documents in many states.

### Tax Exemptions for Section 8 Company

A **Section 8 company income tax exemption** is one of its most attractive features. Upon obtaining **[12A registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/12a-registration)**, the company's income is exempt from tax. With **[80G registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/80g-registration)**, donors can claim deductions on their contributions — making fundraising significantly easier for **social enterprise registration India** initiatives. Explore more at **IndiaFilings [Startup](https://www.indiafilings.com/startup) Services**.

### Credibility and Legal Recognition

Unlike a Trust or Society, a **charitable company India** registered under Section 8 is governed by the stringent provisions of the **Companies Act, 2013**. This brings higher accountability, transparency, and trust among donors, government agencies, and international funding bodies — making it the most credible **non-profit organization India** structure available.

## Who is Eligible to Register a Section 8 Company in India?

Before initiating the **Section 8 company registration process**, it is important to understand the eligibility criteria and **mandatory requirements for Section 8 company registration**.

### Minimum Requirements for Section 8 Company Registration

| Requirement | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Minimum Directors | 2 Directors (at least one must be an Indian resident) |
| Minimum Members | 2 Members (can be same as directors) |
| DIN | All directors must have a [Director Identification Number](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/din-number-registration-search) (DIN) |
| [Digital Signature Certificate](https://www.indiafilings.com/digital-signature) | DSC required for all directors |
| Registered Office | Must have a registered office address in India |
| Minimum Capital | No minimum capital requirement |
| [License](https://www.indiafilings.com/trade-license) | Section 8 License from MCA (Form INC-12) is mandatory |

### Mandatory Requirements for Section 8 Company Registration

- **MCA Name Approval:** The proposed company name must be approved by the MCA through the RUN (Reserve Unique Name) service before filing the incorporation application.
- **MOA & AOA Drafting:** A well-drafted **[Memorandum of Association](https://www.indiafilings.com/memorandum-of-association-amendment) (MOA)** and **[Articles of Association](https://www.indiafilings.com/aoa-amendment) (AOA)** must clearly outline the non-profit objectives and internal governance rules of the company.
- **Company Incorporation:** The company must be formally incorporated through the **[SPICe+ form](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/spice-plus-incorporation)** on the MCA portal after obtaining the Section 8 License.
- **PAN & TAN Registration:** Upon incorporation, the company must obtain a **[Permanent Account Number](https://www.indiafilings.com/pan-card) (PAN)** and **[Tax Deduction Account Number](https://www.indiafilings.com/tan-registration) (TAN)** for all financial and taxation purposes.

### Who Can Be a Director in Section 8 Company?

- Any individual aged 18 years or above
- Must not be of unsound mind or declared insolvent
- Foreign nationals can be directors subject to applicable regulations
- Must obtain DIN from the MCA portal

### Objects Allowed Under Section 8 Company

- Promotion of education, arts, science, or sports
- [Environmental protection](https://www.indiafilings.com/environment-testing) and social welfare activities
- Charity, religion, and community development
- Research and development for public benefit
- Commerce and [trade promotion](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/trade-promotion-scheme) for public benefit

## What Documents Are Required for Section 8 Company Registration?

Having the correct documents ready ensures a smooth **Section 8 company incorporation** process. Below is the complete document checklist:

### Documents Required from Directors/Members

- PAN Card of all directors and members (mandatory)
- Aadhaar Card / Voter ID / Passport / Driving Licence (Identity Proof)
- Bank Statement / Utility Bill (Address Proof – not older than 2 months)
- Passport-size photograph of all directors
- Email ID and mobile number of all directors
- DSC (Digital Signature Certificate) for all directors

### Documents Required for Registered Office

- Latest electricity bill or utility bill of the registered office
- Rent Agreement (if rented) along with NOC from the landlord
- Property ownership documents (if owned by director/member)

### Checklist for Section 8 Company Registration

#### Pre-Registration Checklist

1. Obtain DSC for all directors
2. Apply for DIN for all directors via MCA portal
3. Complete **MCA Name Approval** via RUN (Reserve Unique Name) on MCA portal
4.  Complete **MOA & AOA Drafting** clearly stating the non-profit objectives
5. Prepare declaration and affidavit by proposed directors
6. Apply for Section 8 License (Form INC-12) with required declarations

#### Post-Registration Checklist

1. Complete **Company Incorporation** by filing SPICe+ Form on MCA portal
2. Obtain Certificate of Incorporation from MCA
3. Complete **PAN & TAN Registration** for the company
4. Open a dedicated bank account in the company's name
5. Apply for 12A and 80G registration for tax exemptions
6. Register under FCRA if planning to receive foreign contributions

## What is the Process for Section 8 Company Registration in India?

The **Section 8 company registration process step by step** is entirely online through the MCA portal. Here are the detailed **steps for registration of a Section 8 company**:

### Step 1 – Obtain DSC and DIN for Directors

Every proposed director must first obtain a **Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)** and a **Director Identification Number (DIN)**. The DSC is used to digitally sign all MCA forms, while the DIN is the unique identification number for each director. DIN can be applied via the MCA portal through Form DIR-3.

### Step 2 – MCA Name Approval via RUN

Apply for **MCA Name Approval** through the **RUN (Reserve Unique Name)** service on the MCA portal. The proposed name must reflect the charitable or non-profit nature of the organization. The name must not be identical to any existing company or trademark. This is a critical step before proceeding with **Section 8 company MCA registration**.

### Step 3 – MOA & AOA Drafting and Section 8 License (Form INC-12)

**MOA & AOA Drafting** is a crucial step that defines the objectives, governance, and operational framework of the non-profit company. File **Form INC-12** on the MCA portal along with the draft MOA, AOA, declaration by directors, and estimated income-expenditure statement. Upon review, the MCA issues a **Section 8 License** in **Form INC-16**.

### Step 4 – Company Incorporation via SPICe+ Form

After receiving the Section 8 License, complete **Company Incorporation** by filing the **SPICe+ form** (Simplified Proforma for Incorporating Company Electronically Plus) on the MCA portal. This form integrates DIN allotment, name reservation, **PAN & TAN Registration**, and incorporation application into a single seamless process.

### Step 5 – Receive Certificate of Incorporation

Upon successful verification of all documents and forms, the MCA issues the **Certificate of Incorporation** along with the Company Identification Number (CIN). This officially marks the completion of your **Section 8 company registration online India**.

## What are the 5 Simple Steps to Start a Section 8 Company in India?

Here is a simplified overview of **how to register a Section 8 company in India** in 5 easy steps:

1. **Step 1:** Obtain **DSC and DIN** for all proposed directors from the MCA portal.
2. **Step 2:** Complete **MCA Name Approval** through the RUN service on MCA – ensure the name reflects the non-profit purpose.
3. **Step 3:** Complete **MOA & AOA Drafting** and apply for **Section 8 License** via Form INC-12 with required declarations and income-expenditure projections.
4. **Step 4:** Complete **Company Incorporation** by filing SPICe+ Form on MCA portal after receiving the Section 8 License (Form INC-16).
5. **Step 5:** Receive **Certificate of Incorporation** with CIN and complete **PAN & TAN Registration** – your Section 8 company is now legally registered!

## How Long Does It Take to Register a Section 8 Company?

The time required for **Section 8 company registration** depends on document readiness and MCA processing timelines:

| Stage | Estimated Time |
| --- | --- |
| DSC Procurement | 1–2 Working Days |
| DIN Application | 1–2 Working Days |
| MCA Name Approval (RUN) | 2–3 Working Days |
| MOA & AOA Drafting + Section 8 License (Form INC-12) | 7–10 Working Days |
| Company Incorporation via SPICe+ Filing | 3–5 Working Days |
| PAN & TAN Registration | 1–2 Working Days |
| **Total Estimated Time** | **15–25 Working Days** |

The **Section 8 company registration fees in India** include government fees and professional service charges. Here is a complete breakdown:

### Section 8 Company Registration Fees Table

| Fee Component | Estimated Cost |

| Professional/Service Charges | ₹5,000 – ₹15,000 |
| **Total Estimated Cost** | **₹10,000 – ₹30,000** |

## What are the Compliances After Section 8 Company Registration?

Post incorporation, every **Section 8 company** must fulfil mandatory annual and event-based compliances to maintain its legal standing and tax-exempt status.

### Compliance Requirements for a Section 8 Company

- **Annual General Meeting (AGM):** Must be held within 6 months of the end of each financial year
- **Board Meetings:** Minimum 2 board meetings per year for Section 8 companies
- **Form AOC-4:** Filing of financial statements within 30 days of AGM
- **Form MGT-7:** Annual return filing within 60 days of AGM
- **Income Tax Return:** Filed annually even if income is exempt under 12A
- **Statutory Audit:** Mandatory for all Section 8 companies regardless of turnover
- **FCRA Compliance:** Annual return required if receiving foreign contributions

### Mandatory Compliances for Section 8 Company

| Compliance | Form/Filing | Due Date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Financial Statements Filing | Form AOC-4 | Within 30 days of AGM |
| Annual Return Filing | Form MGT-7 | Within 60 days of AGM |
| Income Tax Return | ITR-7 | 31st October (audit cases) |
| Statutory Audit | Audit Report | Before AGM |
| Director KYC | Form DIR-3 KYC | 30th September every year |
| FCRA Annual Return | FC-4 | 31st December every year |

### Form AOC-4 and MGT-7 Filing

**Form AOC-4** is used for filing the financial statements of the Section 8 company with the MCA. **Form MGT-7** is the Annual Return that captures details of directors, members, and key changes during the financial year. Non-filing of these forms attracts a penalty of **₹100 per day** per form, making timely **Section 8 company annual filing** critical.

### 6 Essential Steps to Avoid Penalties for Section 8 Company

1. Conduct the **Annual General Meeting (AGM)** within the prescribed timeline every year
2. File **Form AOC-4** (Financial Statements) within 30 days after AGM
3. File **Form MGT-7** (Annual Return) within 60 days after AGM
4. Ensure **statutory audit** is completed before AGM every financial year
5. File **Income Tax Return (ITR-7)** before the due date even if income is exempt
6. Complete **Director KYC (Form DIR-3 KYC)** by 30th September every year

## What is the Regulatory Framework for Section 8 Companies in India?

The **Section 8 [company compliance](https://www.indiafilings.com/company-annual-filing)** obligations are governed by multiple laws and regulatory bodies in India:

| Regulatory Body / Law | Role |
| --- | --- |
| Companies Act, 2013 | Primary legislation governing Section 8 company formation and operations |
| Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) | Registration authority and regulatory oversight |
| Income Tax Act, 1961 | Governs 12A, 80G tax exemptions and ITR filing |
| FCRA, 2010 | Governs receipt and utilization of foreign contributions |
| GST Laws | Applicable if turnover exceeds GST registration threshold |
| CSR Rules (Companies Act) | Section 8 companies can receive CSR funds from corporates |

## Frequently asked questions

Common questions aboutSection 8 Company Incorporation Starting at ₹2,899 in India.

What is Section 8 company?

To answer what is Section 8 company, It is a type of not-for-profit company set up for the promotion of art, science, commerce, charity, sports, education, research, or any other useful activity. These companies are typically formed to benefit a specific community or purpose and are excluded from the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 that generally apply to other companies.

Can Section 8 company make profit?

Yes, Section 8 companies can make a profit. Section 8 companies are businesses that receive subsidies from the government to provide services to low-income people. They can also use different ways to gain incomes such as - Investment, Donations, Funding, etc.

What is difference between NGO and Section 8 company?

A Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) is an organization that is independently established and operated, usually with a charitable, educational, religious, or social purpose. NGOs are usually non-profit and do not have a profit motive.

A Section 8 Company is a non-profit organization formed to promote commerce, art, science, sports, education, research, social welfare, religion, charity, protection of environment or any other such object. Section 8 companies are allowed to generate profit but they must use their profits for the purpose of achieving their goals and not for the benefit of its members.

Do I have to be present in-person to incorporate a Section 8 Company?

No, you will not have to be present at our office or appear at any office for the registration of a Section 8 Company. All the documents can be scanned and sent through email to our office. Some documents will also have to be couriered to our office.

What are the documents required for registration?

Identity proof and address proof are mandatory for all the proposed Directors of the Section 8 Company. PAN Card is mandatory for Indian Nationals. In addition, the landlord of the registered office premises must provide a No Objection Certificate for having the registered office in his/her premises and must submit his/her identity proof and address proof.

How long it will take to incorporate a Company?

IndiaFilings.com can incorporate a Section 8 Company for in 20-30 days. The time taken for registration will depend on the submission of relevant documents by the client and the speed of Government Approvals. To ensure speedy registration, please choose a unique name for your Company and ensure you have all the required documents prior to starting the registration process.

How long is the registration of the Company valid?

Once a Company is incorporated, it will be active and in existence as long as the annual compliances are met with regularly. In case, annual compliances are not complied with, the Company will become a Dormant Company and may be struck off from the register after a period of time. A struck-off Company can be revived for a period of up to 20 years.

What is a Digital Signature's Certificate?

A Digital Signature establishes the identity of the sender or signee electronically while filing documents through the Internet. The Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) mandates that the Directors sign some of the application documents using their Digital Signature. Hence, a Digital Signature is required for all Directors of a proposed Section 8 Company.

What is the Director Identification Number?

Director Identification Number is a unique identification number assigned to all existing and proposed Directors of a Company. It is mandatory for all present or proposed Directors to have a Director Identification Number. Director Identification Number never expires and a person can have only one Director Identification Number.

Can NRIs /Foreign Nationals be a Director in a Section 8 Company?

Yes, a NRI or Foreign National can be a Director in a Section 8 Company after obtaining Director Identification Number. However, at least one Director on the Board of Directors must be a Resident India.

How many people are required to register a Private Limited Company?

A minimum of two people is required to register a section 8 company in India.

What are the requirements to be a Director?

The Director needs to be over 18 years of age and must be a natural person. There are no limitations in terms of citizenship or residency. Therefore, even foreign nationals can be Directors in an Indian Section 8 Company.

Is a Physical Office Mandatory to Establish a Section 8 Company?

While a formal office space is not obligatory, a registered address within India is essential for the Section 8 Company. This address can be situated in commercial, industrial, or residential premises, provided it serves as the official communication point with the MCA.
