# GST Registration for Foreigners Online in India

Foreign businesses and non-resident individuals supplying goods or services in India must obtain **GST registration for foreigners** before commencing operations. Stay compliant with Indian tax laws through [GST registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst) for foreigners — fast, simple, and 100% online with IndiaFilings.

## What is GST Registration for Foreigners?

**GST registration for foreigners** is the process by which non-resident businesses or individuals obtain a GSTIN to legally supply goods or services in India. Governed under **Section 27 of the CGST Act, 2017**, it applies to all foreign nationals and companies conducting taxable transactions in India — even temporarily.

- Mandatory before commencing any taxable supply in India
- Governed under Section 27 of CGST Act, 2017
- Valid for 90 days — extendable up to 180 days
- Requires an Indian authorised signatory
- Advance tax deposit mandatory at registration

## Who Needs GST Registration as a Foreigner in India?

The following categories of foreign entities must obtain **non-resident GST registration** in India:

| Category | GST Registration Required? |
| --- | --- |
| **Foreign Companies** supplying goods/services in India | Yes — Mandatory |
| **Non-Resident Individuals** with taxable transactions | Yes — Mandatory |
| **Foreign E-Commerce Operators** | Yes — Mandatory |
| **Foreign Artists / Performers / Exhibitors** | Yes — Mandatory |
| **[Foreign Importers](https://www.indiafilings.com/import-export)** under Reverse Charge | Yes — Mandatory |
| Foreign entities supplying only **exempt goods/services** | Not Required |

## What is a Non-Resident Taxable Person Under GST?

A **Non-Resident Taxable Person (NRTP)** under GST is any person who occasionally undertakes transactions involving the supply of goods or services in India but does not have a fixed place of business or residence in India. The **foreign business GST India** framework specifically caters to such entities under Section 27 of the CGST Act, 2017.

### Key Characteristics of a Non-Resident Taxable Person

- Does not have a fixed place of business in India
- Supplies taxable goods or services in India occasionally
- Must register under GST at least 5 days before commencing business
- Must appoint an authorised representative in India
- Must deposit estimated tax liability in advance

### Difference Between NRTP and Casual Taxable Person

| Parameter | Non-Resident Taxable Person (NRTP) | Casual Taxable Person (CTP) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Residency | Non-resident of India | Resident of India |
| [PAN](https://www.indiafilings.com/pan-card) Requirement | Not Required (Passport accepted) | PAN Mandatory |
| Fixed Business Place in India | Not Required | Required |
| Advance Tax Deposit | Mandatory | Mandatory |
| [ITC](https://www.indiafilings.com/input-tax-credit) Eligibility | Limited | Full ITC Available |
| Validity | 90 days (extendable) | 90 days (extendable) |

Not sure which category applies to you? [GST registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration) experts at IndiaFilings will guide you through the right choice.

## What are the Eligibility Criteria for GST Registration for Foreigners?

Before initiating the **foreigner GST application** process, verify whether your business meets the eligibility criteria for **GST for international businesses**:

### Who Must Register?

- Foreign companies supplying goods or services in India
- Non-resident individuals conducting taxable transactions in India
- Foreign e-commerce operators facilitating supply through digital platforms
- Foreign artists, performers or exhibitors participating in events in India
- Foreign importers of services liable under reverse charge mechanism

### Who is Exempt from GST Registration?

- Foreign entities supplying only exempt goods or services
- Foreign businesses with no taxable supply in India
- Entities covered under specific GST exemption notifications
- Foreign diplomatic missions and UN bodies with specific exemptions

## What Documents are Required for GST Registration for Foreigners?

Keep these **[GST registration documents for foreigners](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/foreign-non-resident-taxpayer-gst-registration-documents-required)** ready before starting your application:

| Document | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Passport | Valid passport of the foreign applicant (replaces PAN) |
| Tax Identification Number | TIN issued by home country |
| Proof of Business | Certificate of incorporation from home country |
| Authorised Signatory Details | PAN, [Aadhaar](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/eaadhaar-download) and address proof of Indian representative |
| Bank Account Details | Indian bank account of authorised representative |
| Proof of Business Address | Address proof of temporary business location in India |
| Advance Tax Deposit Proof | Challan of advance tax deposited |
| Board Resolution / POA | Authorization letter appointing Indian representative |

If you are exporting goods or services, explore [GST LUT](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-lut) filing to supply without payment of IGST.

## How to Apply for GST Registration as a Foreigner in India?

Follow these simple steps to complete your **[foreigner GST application](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-registration-non-resident-taxable-person)** seamlessly:

1. **Step 1 — Appoint Indian Authorised Signatory:** Designate a resident Indian with valid PAN and Aadhaar as your representative.
2. **Step 2 — Collect Documents:** Gather all required **documents required for foreign GST** including passport and TIN.
3. **Step 3 — Calculate and [Deposit Advance Tax](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/deposit-gst-registration):** Estimate GST liability and deposit advance tax in the Electronic Cash Ledger.
4. **Step 4 — Visit GST Portal:** Go to www.gst.gov.in and navigate to Services → Registration → New Registration.
5. **Step 5 — Select NRTP Category:** Choose Non-Resident Taxable Person as taxpayer type.
6. **Step 6 — Fill Form [GST REG-09](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/gst-registration-non-resident-taxable-person):** Complete the application with passport details and Indian business address.
7. **Step 7 — Upload Documents:** Upload all documents in prescribed formats on the portal.
8. **Step 8 — Submit and Get GSTIN:** Submit via DSC or [EVC](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/what-is-evc-in-income-tax-return) and receive your **GSTIN for foreign nationals** upon approval.

Use [GST search](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-search) to verify your GSTIN details after approval.

## What is the Validity and Renewal of GST Registration for Foreigners?

| Parameter | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Initial Validity | 90 days from effective date of registration |
| Extension Period | Additional 90 days (maximum 180 days total) |
| Extension Form | GST REG-11 — filed before initial period expires |
| Additional Tax Deposit | Required at the time of extension |
| Cancellation | Via [GST revocation](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-revocation) or auto-expiry after validity period |

For long-term operations, consider a permanent [GST registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration) through a subsidiary. Manage changes via [GST amendment](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-amendment) services.

## What are the GST Compliance Obligations for Foreigners?

Once registered, foreign businesses must fulfil the following **GST compliance for overseas companies** requirements:

- File **GSTR-5** monthly within 13 days after end of each tax period
- File **GSTR-5A** for OIDAR service providers
- Issue [GST e-invoice](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-einvoice) for all applicable B2B transactions
- Claim [GST refund](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-refund) on excess tax paid or accumulated ITC
- File [GST return filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-return-filing) before applying for cancellation
- Respond promptly to any [GST notice](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-notice) from authorities
- File [GST annual return](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-annual-return) if applicable based on turnover
- Comply with [income tax](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax) obligations alongside GST requirements
- Explore [startup India](https://www.indiafilings.com/startup) benefits if launching a new venture
- Consider [MCA services](https://www.indiafilings.com/mca-services) for company incorporation in India

## Why IndiaFilings is the Best Choice for Non-Resident GST Compliance?

Thousands of foreign businesses and **non-resident taxable persons** trust IndiaFilings for end-to-end **GST compliance for overseas companies**. Our dedicated team of qualified Chartered Accountants ensures your **non-resident GST registration** is completed accurately, on time, and without any compliance gaps.

From appointing your authorised signatory to filing **GSTR-5 returns**, managing GST amendments, and handling GST notices — IndiaFilings provides complete support at every stage of your **GST for international businesses** journey in India.

Whether you need GST refund assistance, [GST return filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-return-filing), or guidance on [GST LUT](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-lut) for exports — our experts are always available to guide you through every compliance requirement.

With a **pan-India presence**, **transparent pricing**, and a proven track record of serving **5,000+ foreign clients**, IndiaFilings is the most trusted partner for **foreigner GST application** and ongoing compliance in India.

Get started today with [GST registration for foreigners](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-registration-for-foreigners) and let our experts handle everything — so you can focus on growing your business in India.

## Frequently asked questions

Common questions aboutGST Registration for Foreigners & Non Resident Taxable Persons.

Who needs to register under GST in India?

Any foreign individual or entity supplying goods or services in India without a permanent establishment or residence must register under GST.

What is a Non-Resident Taxable Person?

A Non-Resident Taxable Person is an entity conducting transactions in India without a fixed place of business or residence within the country.

Is GST registration mandatory for non-residents?

Yes, GST registration is compulsory for non-resident taxable persons, irrespective of their transaction volume.

Can non-resident taxable persons opt for composition levy?

No, non-resident taxable persons are not eligible for the composition levy scheme under GST.

How soon should GST registration be done?

GST registration must be completed at least five days before commencing business operations in India.

What documents are required for GST registration?

Documents include proof of authorized signatory, proof of principal place of business, and proof of details of bank accounts, among others.

What is the validity period of NRI GST registration?

The registration is valid for the specified period in the application or ninety days from the effective date, whichever is earlier.

What are the phases of GST registration for NRIs?

The process includes provisional registration and final registration.

Which form is used for provisional GST registration?

Form GST REG-09 is used for provisional registration by NRIs.

How is the GST registration application submitted?

The application is submitted electronically through the official GST portal along with a self-attested copy of the applicant's valid passport.

What is the significance of the advance tax deposit?

An advance tax deposit equivalent to the estimated tax liability must be made before the registration certificate is issued, ensuring compliance.

How is final registration under GST obtained?

Final registration is obtained by submitting Form GST REG–26 electronically with the necessary information furnished within three months.

What happens if there are discrepancies in the application?

Discrepancies may lead to a show-cause notice, and the applicant will be given an opportunity to rectify.

Who can act as the authorized signatory for NRIs?

An authorized signatory must be a resident of India with a valid PAN, acting on behalf of the NRI for GST compliance.

What is the procedure for extending GST registration validity?

An extension application using Form GST REG-11 must be filed before the current registration expires, along with an additional advance tax deposit.

Are non-resident taxable persons eligible for input tax credit?

Non-resident taxable persons cannot claim input tax credit except for directly imported goods; however, the taxes paid can be utilized as a credit by the recipients.

How are GST returns filed by non-residents?

Non-residents must electronically submit GST returns using Form GSTR-5, including details of outward and inward supplies, and pay applicable taxes within the stipulated timeframe.

When can a refund of advance tax be claimed?

Refund of advance tax is eligible after submitting all necessary returns for the duration of registration validity, with the application made in Form GSTR-5, Section 13.

What support does IndiaFilings offer for NRI GST registration?

IndiaFilings provides expert guidance, streamlined application processes, assistance with authorized signatories, timely submissions, and ongoing support for GST compliance.

How can one connect with IndiaFilings for assistance?

Interested individuals or entities can connect with IndiaFilings to streamline GST registration by contacting their expert team.

Do I need to charge GST to foreign clients India?

Most taxpayers are confused over the question, 'Do I need to charge GST to foreign clients India'. If you are providing services to foreign clients in India, you generally do not need to charge GST. According to the GST regulations, if you receive payment in a foreign currency and meet specific conditions, your services are considered zero-rated exports.

How can I do GST registration documents download?

You can complete the GST registration documents download from the official GST portal. The portal provides access to all necessary forms and guidelines related to GST registration, including FORM GST REG-09 for non-resident taxable persons and other supporting documents required for different types of applicants.

File ADT-1 online with MCA for auditor appointment or reappointment. We manage documentation, resolutions, and timely filing to ensure full compliance under the Companies Act, 2013.

# ADT-1 Filing Online in India for Companies

**ADT-1 filing online in India** is a mandatory compliance requirement under the Companies Act 2013. Every company registered in India must file **Form ADT-1** to intimate the Registrar of Companies (ROC) about the appointment of its statutory auditor. Whether it is a first-time appointment or a reappointment after an Annual General Meeting (AGM), timely [ADT-1 filing online](https://www.indiafilings.com/adt-1-filing/adt1-filing-online-a-complete-guide-for-companies) ensures your company stays compliant with MCA regulations and avoids unnecessary penalties.

## What is ADT-1 Form Filing in India?

Form ADT-1 is an official intimation submitted by a company to the Registrar of Companies (ROC) regarding the appointment or reappointment of a statutory auditor. It is governed under Section 139 of the Companies Act 2013 and is a critical part of **auditor appointment MCA** compliance. Filing this form ensures transparency in corporate governance and keeps the MCA records updated with the latest auditor details.

### Form ADT-1 serves as a formal notification to the ROC that a company has appointed or reappointed an auditor. It must be filed within 15 days of the AGM or Board Meeting where the auditor was appointed.

- Governed under Companies Act 2013, Section 139
- Filed on MCA21 portal online
- Applicable to all registered companies in India
- Required for both first-time and subsequent auditor appointments

### Legal Framework under Companies Act 2013

The legal basis for ADT-1 filing is rooted in the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules 2014. Rule 4 specifically mandates that every company must file **Form ADT-1** with the ROC within the prescribed time limit. Non-compliance attracts significant penalties under the Act.

## What is the ADT-1 Due Date for Companies in India?

Understanding the **ADT-1 due date** is essential for every company to avoid late fees and penalties. The **ADT-1 time limit** varies depending on the type of auditor appointment — whether it is a first appointment by the Board of Directors or a reappointment at the AGM. Missing the deadline can result in significant financial penalties and compliance issues.

### Due Date for New Companies

For newly incorporated companies, the Board of Directors appoints the first auditor within 30 days of incorporation. The **ADT-1 Form** must be filed within 15 days of this Board Meeting.

- Board appointment: Within 30 days of incorporation
- ADT-1 filing deadline: Within 15 days of Board Meeting
- Casual vacancy appointment: Within 15 days of Board Meeting

### Due Date After AGM

For companies reappointing or appointing a new auditor at the AGM, the **ADT-1 due date** is within 15 days from the conclusion of the AGM. Companies must ensure timely submission to avoid **ADT-1 late fees**.

| Event | ADT-1 Filing Deadline |
| --- | --- |
| First Auditor Appointment (Board) | Within 15 days of Board Meeting |
| Auditor Appointment/Reappointment at AGM | Within 15 days of AGM |
| Casual Vacancy Filling | Within 15 days of Board Meeting |

### ADT-1 Time Limit for Filing

The **ADT-1 time limit** is strictly 15 days from the date of the meeting where the auditor was appointed. Companies that miss this window must file with additional [ADT-1 late fees](https://www.indiafilings.com/adt-1-filing/form-adt1-due-date--late-fees-guide) as prescribed by the MCA.

## Who Needs to File Form ADT-1 in India?

Understanding the [ADT-1 applicability](https://www.indiafilings.com/adt-1-filing/applicability) is critical for corporate compliance. Not all entities are required to file this form, but every registered company under the Companies Act 2013 must comply. Knowing who is liable helps avoid penalties and keeps the company in good standing with the ROC.

### Applicability for Private Limited Companies

All private limited companies registered under the Companies Act 2013 must file **Form ADT-1** every time they appoint or reappoint a statutory auditor. This includes companies appointing their first auditor after incorporation.

### Applicability for Public Limited Companies

Public limited companies are also mandatorily required to file ADT-1. Given the higher level of public interest involved, compliance with **ROC ADT-1 filing** is strictly monitored by regulatory authorities.

### Entities Not Required to File ADT-1

- One Person Companies (OPCs) — exempted from ADT-1 filing
- Small companies — exempted under certain conditions
- LLPs — not governed under Companies Act 2013
- Partnership firms — not applicable

## What Are the Features of ADT-1 Filing in India?

The **ADT-1 filing online** process comes with several important features that make it a structured and transparent compliance mechanism under the MCA framework. Understanding these features helps companies prepare and submit the form efficiently without errors or delays.

### Key Features of ADT-1 Filing

- Filed entirely online on the MCA21 portal
- Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) of the director is mandatory
- Applicable for appointment, reappointment, and casual vacancy
- **ADT-1 Form pdf** available for download on the MCA portal
- Acknowledgement generated instantly upon successful submission
- SRN (Service Request Number) issued for tracking status

### Auditor Appointment Benefits

Filing ADT-1 on time ensures that the **company auditor appointment** is officially recorded with the ROC. This protects the company from compliance risks and strengthens its corporate governance structure.

### MCA Compliance Significance

Regular and timely **MCA ADT-1 submission** demonstrates a company's commitment to transparency and statutory compliance, which is essential for raising funds, obtaining loans, and maintaining investor confidence.

## What is the ADT-1 Form PDF and How to Download It in India?

The **ADT-1 Form pdf** is the official document prescribed by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) for intimating auditor appointments. Companies can download the [ADT-1 Form pdf](https://www.indiafilings.com/adt-1-filing/download-form) directly from the MCA portal and fill it with the required auditor and company details before submission.

### Steps to Download ADT-1 Form PDF from MCA Portal

1. Visit the official MCA portal at mca.gov.in
2. Navigate to "MCA Services" and click on "e-Filing"
3. Search for "Form ADT-1" under the list of company forms
4. Download the latest version of the **ADT-1 Form pdf**
5. Open the form using Adobe Acrobat Reader
6. Fill in the company CIN, auditor details, and appointment date
7. Attach required documents and affix DSC
8. Upload and submit on the MCA21 portal

### Steps to Fill ADT-1 Form

While filling the **Form ADT-1**, ensure you enter the correct Corporate Identification Number (CIN), auditor's membership number, date of appointment, and financial year details. Any mismatch may result in rejection of the filing.

## What Documents Are Required for ADT-1 Filing in India?

Preparing the right set of documents is crucial for a smooth **ADT-1 online filing process**. Incomplete documentation is one of the most common reasons for rejection of ADT-1 submissions on the MCA portal. Refer to the complete [documents required for ADT-1](https://www.indiafilings.com/adt-1-filing/documents-required) filing checklist below.

### List of Documents Required

- Board Resolution for auditor appointment
- Auditor's written consent to act as auditor
- Certificate from auditor confirming eligibility under Companies Act
- Company's Certificate of Incorporation
- Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) of the authorized director
- PAN and membership number of the auditor/audit firm

### Auditor Consent Letter

The auditor's consent letter is a mandatory attachment to **Form ADT-1**. It confirms that the auditor has agreed to the appointment and meets all eligibility criteria under Section 141 of the Companies Act 2013.

### Board Resolution

A certified copy of the Board Resolution or AGM Resolution authorizing the auditor appointment must be attached. This is a critical document for **ROC ADT-1 filing** and must be certified by a Company Secretary or Director.

## How Does the ADT-1 Filing Process Work Online in India?

The **ADT-1 filing online** process is entirely digital and managed through the MCA21 portal. Companies can complete the entire process without visiting any government office. Follow this step-by-step approach for a hassle-free [ADT-1 filing process](https://www.indiafilings.com/adt-1-filing/adt1-filing-process-stepbystep-guide).

### Step-by-Step Online Process

1. **Login to MCA21 Portal:** Use your registered credentials to log in
2. **Select Form ADT-1:** Navigate to "e-Filing" and select Form ADT-1
3. **Enter Company Details:** Fill in CIN, company name, and registered office address
4. **Fill Auditor Details:** Enter auditor name, membership number, and firm registration number
5. **Enter Appointment Details:** Mention date of appointment and type of appointment
6. **Attach Documents:** Upload Board Resolution, consent letter, and eligibility certificate
7. **Affix DSC:** Attach the Digital Signature Certificate of the authorized director
8. **Pay Filing Fees:** Pay the applicable **ADT-1 fees** online
9. **Submit Form:** Submit the form and note the SRN for tracking

### MCA21 Portal Filing Tips

Ensure that the company's MCA account is active and the DSC is valid before initiating the **ADT-1 form submission online**. Always check the form version compatibility with the MCA portal before uploading.

## What Are the ADT-1 Late Fees and Penalty in India?

Missing the **ADT-1 due date** results in additional **ADT-1 late fees** and potential penalties under the Companies Act 2013. It is important for companies to understand the penalty structure and use an **ADT-1 penalty calculator** to estimate their liability before filing.

### ADT-1 Late Fees Structure

| Delay Period | Late Fees Applicable |
| --- | --- |
| Up to 30 days | 2x of normal filing fees |
| More than 30 days up to 60 days | 4x of normal filing fees |
| More than 60 days up to 90 days | 6x of normal filing fees |
| More than 90 days up to 180 days | 10x of normal filing fees |
| Beyond 180 days | 12x of normal filing fees |

### ADT-1 Penalty Calculator

Companies can use the **ADT-1 penalty calculator** available on the MCA portal to estimate the exact late fees payable based on the number of days delayed. This helps in planning the [ADT-1 form revision](https://www.indiafilings.com/adt-1-filing/can-form-be-revised) and payment before submission.

### Penalty for Non-Compliance

Beyond late fees, continued non-compliance with **ADT-1 compliance India** requirements can result in:

- Penalty on the company: Up to Rs. 50,000
- Penalty on every officer in default: Up to Rs. 50,000
- Disqualification of directors in extreme cases

## How Much Does ADT-1 Filing Cost in India?

The **ADT-1 fees** depend on the company's paid-up share capital. The government filing fees are relatively modest, but professional charges for expert assistance may vary based on the complexity of the filing. Below is a structured breakdown of the **ADT-1 filing fees and professional charges India**.

### ADT-1 Government Fees Structure

| Paid-Up Share Capital | Government Filing Fee |
| --- | --- |
| Less than Rs. 1,00,000 | Rs. 200 |
| Rs. 1,00,000 to Rs. 4,99,999 | Rs. 300 |
| Rs. 5,00,000 to Rs. 24,99,999 | Rs. 400 |
| Rs. 25,00,000 to Rs. 99,99,999 | Rs. 500 |
| Rs. 1,00,00,000 or more | Rs. 600 |

### Professional Charges

Professional assistance for **ADT-1 filing online India** typically ranges from Rs. 500 to Rs. 2,000 depending on the service provider. Expert assistance ensures error-free filing and timely submission, saving companies from unnecessary **ADT-1 late fees**.

## How Does ADT-1 Filing Differ from ADT-3 in India?

Many companies confuse **Form ADT-1** with Form ADT-3. While both are related to statutory auditors, they serve entirely different purposes under the Companies Act 2013. Understanding the difference helps companies file the correct form and avoid compliance errors.

### ADT-1 vs ADT-3 Comparison

| Parameter | Form ADT-1 | Form ADT-3 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Purpose | Intimation of auditor appointment | Intimation of auditor resignation |
| Filed By | Company | Auditor |
| Time Limit | 15 days from appointment | 30 days from resignation |
| Applicable Event | Appointment / Reappointment | Resignation of auditor |
| Portal | MCA21 | MCA21 |

IndiaFilings is India's leading business compliance platform, trusted by thousands of companies for seamless **ADT-1 compliance India** services. Our expert team handles every aspect of the filing process — from document preparation to final submission — ensuring zero errors and timely delivery.

Our professionals are well-versed with MCA regulations and stay updated with the latest changes in **auditor appointment MCA** requirements. We provide end-to-end support, making the entire **ADT-1 online filing process** smooth and stress-free for company directors and compliance officers.

With transparent pricing, dedicated support, and a proven track record, IndiaFilings ensures your **company auditor filing** is completed accurately and on time — every time. Trust us to manage your MCA compliance while you focus on growing your business.

Ready to file your ADT-1 form without hassle? Get started with expert assistance today. [**File ADT-1 Online with IndiaFilings**](https://www.indiafilings.com/adt-1-filing) and ensure your company stays fully compliant with MCA regulations.

## Frequently asked questions

Common questions aboutADT-1 Form Filing Online for Auditor Appointment India.

What is Form ADT-1?

Form ADT-1 is a statutory return filed with the Registrar of Companies (ROC) to report the appointment or reappointment of an auditor as per Section 139 of the Companies Act, 2013.

Who is responsible for filing Form ADT-1?

The company is responsible for filing Form ADT-1, not the auditor.

Is Form ADT-1 required for the appointment of the first auditor?

Yes, under the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Amendment Rules, 2025, filing ADT-1 is now mandatory for first auditor appointments, including those made by the Board of Directors.

When should Form ADT-1 be filed?

It must be filed within 15 days of the auditor's appointment, whether it occurs at the Board Meeting or AGM.

What happens if I miss the ADT-1 filing deadline?

Late filing attracts penalties, with fees increasing based on the number of days delayed.

What is the penalty for late filing of Form ADT-1?

Penalty ranges from 2x to 12x the normal filing fee, depending on the delay period.

What are the documents required for filing Form ADT-1?

**Key documents include:**

- Copy of Board/AGM resolution
- Auditor's consent letter
- Certificate under Section 141
- Intimation sent to auditor

What details of the auditor are required in Form ADT-1?

**You need to provide the auditor’s:**

- Name and address
- PAN and membership number
- Email and contact info
- Period of appointment
- Firm registration number (if applicable)

Is Form ADT-1 applicable to all companies?

Yes, it is mandatory for all types of companies—private, public, listed, unlisted, and OPCs.

Is Form ADT-1 applicable for casual vacancy appointments?

Yes, companies must file ADT-1 even when an auditor is appointed to fill a casual vacancy.

What is the filing fee for Form ADT-1?

The fee ranges from ₹200 to ₹600, based on the company’s nominal share capital.

Where can I file Form ADT-1?

Form ADT-1 is filed online through the MCA (Ministry of Corporate Affairs) portal.

Do I need a digital signature for filing Form ADT-1?

Yes, the form must be digitally signed by a Director and a practicing professional (CA/CS/CMA).

What is the due date for newly incorporated companies?

Within 15 days of appointing the first auditor, which must happen within 30 days of incorporation—effectively making the due date within 45 days of incorporation.

Can IndiaFilings help with ADT-1 filing?

Yes, we at IndiaFilings provide complete support for Form ADT-1 filing—from preparing necessary documents to submitting the form online and ensuring full legal compliance.

Can I revise Form ADT-1 after submission?

You cannot revise it directly; however, in case of an error, a new filing or clarification may be submitted via ROC after consultation.

Is the filing of ADT-1 auto-approved?

Yes, if all details and documents are accurate, the form is typically auto-approved by the MCA system.

Is Form ADT-1 required for reappointment of the same auditor?

Yes, reappointment at the AGM still requires Form ADT-1 to be filed within 15 days.

What happens if the form is rejected due to errors?

You may need to resubmit the form with corrections, possibly with additional filing fees depending on the delay.

What’s the easiest way to stay compliant with Form ADT-1 filing?

The easiest way is to rely on our expert team at IndiaFilings. We handle the end-to-end process, ensure accuracy, prevent delays, and keep your company 100% compliant with MCA regulations.

# Business Loan Online in India – Quick & Easy Financing Solutions

A **business loan online in India** is one of the fastest and most convenient ways to secure funds for your enterprise. Whether you are a startup, MSME, or an established company, [IndiaFilings](https://www.indiafilings.com/) helps you access the right **business funding** with minimal documentation and quick approval.

What is a Business Loan?

A **business loan** is a financial product offered by banks, NBFCs, and fintech platforms to help businesses meet their operational, expansion, or capital requirements. It is a form of **commercial loan** that provides lump-sum funding repaid over a fixed tenure with interest. In India, **business finance** solutions are available for MSMEs, startups, traders, manufacturers, and large enterprises alike.

Whether you need funds for purchasing equipment, managing cash flow, or scaling operations, a **loan for business** gives you the financial leverage to achieve your goals without diluting equity. Businesses can opt for [**secured loans**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/secured-loan) or [**unsecured loans**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/unsecured-loan) depending on their eligibility and collateral availability.

## What is the Purpose of a Business Loan?

Understanding the purpose of a **business loan online in India** helps businesses make informed borrowing decisions. From scaling operations to managing short-term liquidity, **enterprise loans** serve multiple purposes across industries.

### Business Expansion Loan

A [**business expansion loan**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/business-expansion-loan) is designed to help businesses scale their operations, enter new markets, or open new branches. It provides long-term capital to fuel growth with structured repayment plans. This is one of the most sought-after forms of **business funding** for growing SMEs.

### Loan Against Property

A [**loan against property**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/loan-against-property) allows business owners to leverage their residential or commercial property as collateral to access high-value loans at competitive interest rates. It is ideal for businesses requiring large capital infusion for long-term projects.

### Inventory Financing

**Inventory financing** is a short-term **business credit** solution that allows businesses to purchase inventory in bulk without straining their cash flow. It is particularly beneficial for traders, retailers, and manufacturers who need to maintain optimal stock levels during peak seasons.

### Export Finance

**Export finance** helps Indian businesses involved in international trade to fund their export operations. It covers pre-shipment and post-shipment credit requirements, ensuring smooth execution of export orders. Solutions like [**letter of credit**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/letter-of-credit) and [**bank guarantee**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/bank-guarantee) are widely used in export finance.

## What are the Types of Business Loans Available in India?

India offers a wide variety of **business loan** products catering to different financial needs. Here is an overview of the most popular types of **SME loans** and **MSME loans** available today:

### Term Loan

A [**term loan**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/term-loan) is a lump-sum loan disbursed for a fixed period, repaid through EMIs. It is best suited for capital expenditure such as purchasing assets, expanding infrastructure, or funding large projects. Term loans can be short-term (up to 1 year), medium-term (1–5 years), or long-term (above 5 years).

### Working Capital Loan

A [**working capital loan**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/working-capital-loan) is designed to finance the day-to-day operational expenses of a business. It covers salary payments, vendor payments, utility bills, and inventory purchases. This is one of the most common forms of **business finance** for MSMEs.

### Overdraft Facility

An [**overdraft facility**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/overdraft-facility) allows businesses to withdraw funds beyond their account balance up to a pre-approved limit. Interest is charged only on the amount utilised, making it a flexible and cost-effective **business credit** option for managing short-term cash flow gaps.

### Unsecured Loan

An [**unsecured loan**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/unsecured-loan) does not require any collateral or security. It is based entirely on the borrower's creditworthiness and business performance. **Collateral-free loans** are popular among small businesses and startups that do not have significant assets to pledge.

### Secured Loan

A [**secured loan**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/secured-loan) requires the borrower to pledge an asset as collateral. In return, businesses benefit from lower interest rates and higher loan amounts. Properties, machinery, and financial assets are commonly used as security for secured business loans.

### Machinery Loan

A [**machinery loan**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/machinery-loan) is specifically designed to help businesses purchase new or used machinery. It enables manufacturers and industrialists to upgrade their production capabilities without impacting their working capital. The machinery itself often serves as collateral.

### Equipment Loan

An [**equipment loan**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/equipment-loan) helps businesses acquire essential equipment required for operations. From IT hardware to medical devices and construction equipment, this loan type covers a wide range of asset classes and is repaid through structured EMIs over the equipment's useful life.

### Invoice Financing

[**Invoice financing**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/invoice-financing) allows businesses to borrow against their outstanding invoices to improve cash flow. Instead of waiting for clients to pay, businesses can get immediate access to funds. It is an ideal **working capital finance** solution for B2B businesses with long payment cycles.

### Bill Discounting

[**Bill discounting**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/bill-discounting) is a short-term borrowing method where a business sells its trade bills to a lender at a discount to get immediate liquidity. It is widely used in trade finance and helps businesses maintain uninterrupted cash flow during credit periods.

### Letter of Credit

A [**letter of credit**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/letter-of-credit) is a financial instrument issued by a bank guaranteeing that a buyer's payment to a seller will be received on time and in full. It is commonly used in domestic and international trade to reduce payment risk and build trust between trading parties.

### Bank Guarantee

A [**bank guarantee**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/bank-guarantee) is a commitment by a bank to cover a loss if a borrower defaults on a contract. It assures the beneficiary that the bank will honour the obligation if the applicant fails to meet their contractual duties, making it vital for government tenders and large contracts.

## What are the Types of Business Loans for Different Business Entities?

Different business structures have unique financial needs. Here is a breakdown of **business loan options** available for various types of business entities in India:

### Startup Loan

A [**startup loan**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/startup-loan) provides early-stage businesses with the capital required to launch, develop products, and scale operations. Government-backed schemes like [**CGTMSE**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/cgtmse) and [**CGSS**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/cgss) offer collateral-free funding for eligible startups.

### Small Business Loan

A [**small business loan**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/small-business-loan) is tailored for micro and small enterprises that require limited funding for operations, inventory, or expansion. These loans are available through banks, NBFCs, and government schemes with minimal documentation requirements.

### Women Entrepreneur Loan

A [**women entrepreneur loan**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/women-entrepreneur-loan) is a specially curated **business loan for women** business owners in India. These loans come with preferential interest rates, relaxed eligibility norms, and government-backed guarantees to encourage female entrepreneurship across sectors.

### Proprietorship Loan

A [**proprietorship loan**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/proprietorship-loan) is designed for sole proprietors who need business financing. Since the business and owner are legally the same entity, lenders assess both personal and business financials to determine eligibility and loan amount.

### Partnership Firm Loan

A [**partnership firm loan**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/partnership-firm-loan) enables registered partnership firms to access business credit for operational or expansion needs. Lenders typically require the partnership deed, financial statements, and KYC documents of all partners for loan processing.

### Private Limited Company Loan

A [**private limited company loan**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/private-limited-company-loan) offers corporate entities structured financing with higher loan limits. Companies with strong financials and credit ratings can access competitive interest rates and flexible repayment terms from banks and NBFCs.

### Trader Loan

A [**trader loan**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/trader-loan) is a customised **business finance** product for retail and wholesale traders. It helps them manage inventory purchases, seasonal demands, and working capital requirements efficiently with quick disbursal and minimal documentation.

### Manufacturer Loan

A [**manufacturer loan**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/manufacturer-loan) caters to manufacturing businesses that need capital for raw materials, machinery upgrades, plant expansion, or operational expenses. It supports the growth of the manufacturing sector under initiatives like Make in India.

## What are the Features and Benefits of a Business Loan Online in India?

Applying for a **business loan online in India** comes with several advantages that make it a preferred **business funding** option for entrepreneurs and MSMEs:

- **Collateral-Free Options:** Many lenders offer **unsecured business loans** without requiring any asset as security.
- **Quick Disbursal:** With digital processes, **instant business loans** can be disbursed within 24–72 hours of approval.
- **Flexible Repayment:** Choose repayment tenures ranging from 12 months to 84 months based on your cash flow.
- **Competitive Interest Rates:** **Business loan interest rates** start from as low as 10% per annum depending on the lender and profile.
- **High Loan Amounts:** Access funding from ₹1 Lakh to ₹10 Crore based on eligibility.
- **Minimal Documentation:** Online applications require basic KYC, bank statements, and business registration documents.
- **Multiple Loan Types:** From [**cash credit**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/cash-credit) to term loans, choose the product best suited to your needs.
- **Government-Backed Schemes:** Benefit from schemes like CGTMSE and CGSS for collateral-free credit guarantees.

## Who is Eligible for a Business Loan Online in India?

Lenders assess several parameters before approving a **business loan application**. Here are the general eligibility criteria for a **business loan in India**:

| Parameter | Eligibility Criteria |
| --- | --- |
| Business Type | Proprietorship, Partnership, LLP, Private Limited Company, Public Limited Company |
| Business Vintage | Minimum 1–3 years in operation (varies by lender) |
| Annual Turnover | Minimum ₹10 Lakhs per annum (varies by lender) |
| Applicant Age | 21 to 65 years at the time of loan maturity |
| Credit Score | CIBIL score of 700 and above preferred |
| Profitability | Business should be profit-making for the last 1–2 years |
| Nationality | Indian Resident or Indian-owned business entity |

## What Documents are Required for a Business Loan Online in India?

To apply for a **business loan online in India**, you need to submit the following documents. Having these ready speeds up the **business loan approval** process significantly:

1. **KYC Documents:** Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Passport, or Voter ID of the applicant/directors
2. **Business Registration Proof:** GST Certificate, Udyam Registration, MSME Certificate, or Shop Act Licence
3. **Financial Statements:** ITR for the last 2–3 years, audited balance sheets, and profit & loss statements
4. **Bank Statements:** Last 6–12 months of business bank account statements
5. **Business Address Proof:** Utility bills, rent agreement, or property ownership documents
6. **Ownership Documents:** Partnership deed, MOA/AOA for companies, or proprietorship declaration
7. **Collateral Documents:** Property papers or asset documents (for secured loans only)

## What are the Interest Rates and Charges for Business Loans in India?

The **business loan interest rate** in India varies depending on the lender type, loan amount, tenure, and applicant profile. Here is a comparative overview:

| Lender Type | Interest Rate (Per Annum) | Processing Fee | Loan Amount |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Public Sector Banks | 10% – 14% | 0.5% – 1% | Up to ₹10 Crore |
| Private Sector Banks | 12% – 18% | 1% – 2% | Up to ₹5 Crore |
| NBFCs | 15% – 24% | 2% – 3% | Up to ₹2 Crore |
| Fintech Lenders | 18% – 36% | 2% – 4% | Up to ₹50 Lakhs |
| Government Schemes (CGTMSE/CGSS) | 8% – 12% | Nil – 0.5% | Up to ₹5 Crore |

## How to Apply for a Business Loan Online in India?

Applying for a **business loan online in India** has become simpler than ever with digital lending platforms, banks, and NBFCs offering end-to-end online processes. Here is a step-by-step guide to help you through the **business loan application** process:

1. **Step 1 – Identify Your Loan Requirement:** Determine the type of **business funding** you need — whether it is a [**term loan**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/term-loan), [**working capital loan**](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-loan/working-capital-loan), or any other **commercial loan** product.
2. **Step 2 – Check Your Eligibility:** Review the lender's eligibility criteria including business vintage, annual turnover, **CIBIL score**, and business type before applying for a **business loan online**.
3. **Step 3 – Compare Lenders:** Compare **business loan interest rates**, processing fees, repayment tenures, and loan amounts across banks, NBFCs, and fintech platforms to find the **best business loan** for your needs.
4. **Step 4 – Gather Required Documents:** Prepare all necessary documents including KYC proof, **business registration** documents, financial statements, and bank statements to support your **business loan application**.
5. **Step 5 – Fill the Online Application:** Visit the lender's website or platform and fill in the **online business loan** application form with accurate business and personal details.
6. **Step 6 – Submit Documents:** Upload all required documents digitally. Ensure all documents are valid, clear, and up to date to avoid delays in **business loan approval**.
7. **Step 7 – Loan Processing & Verification:** The lender will review your application, verify documents, and assess your **business credit** profile. This may take anywhere from a few hours to a few days.
8. **Step 8 – Loan Approval & Disbursal:** Once approved, the **instant business loan** amount is disbursed directly to your registered business bank account, often within 24–72 hours.

## Why Should You Use IndiaFilings for Business Loan Online in India?

**IndiaFilings** simplifies your **business loan** journey with expert guidance, a wide lender network, and end-to-end support — from eligibility check to final disbursal. Get the right **business funding** solution tailored to your needs, quickly and transparently.

# Certificate of Commencement of Business​

Is your company incorporated and having share capital? One crucial compliance that must be completed before starting business operations is the declaration of the Commencement of Business. Yes, obtaining the Certificate of Commencement of Business (COB) is mandatory for companies incorporated with share capital after November 2, 2018.

At IndiaFilings, we not only assist with company registration but also specialize in guiding businesses through various compliance requirements with ease and precision. From initial company registration to securing the COB Certificate and managing ongoing compliances, we provide a comprehensive range of services to ensure your business adheres to all statutory norms and regulations.

## What is Commencement of Business?

The Commencement of Business is a formal declaration made by the directors of a company within 180 days of its incorporation. This declaration confirms that the subscribers to the Memorandum of Association (MOA) have paid the agreed value of shares, and it includes verification of the company’s registered office address. The declaration, along with proof of the subscription money received, must be filed using Form 20A with the Registrar of Companies (RoC) . Compliance with this requirement is essential for companies to legally commence their business operations.  All this critical information constitutes the commencement of business meaning.

Verification of  Form 20A is conducted by authorised professionals such as Chartered Accountants (CA), Company Secretaries (CS), or Cost Accountants (CWA). Errors or discrepancies in the submitted commencement of business form can lead to accountability for these professionals, resulting in penalties under the Companies Act 2013.

## Who needs to file a declaration for the Commencement of Business?

Under the Companies Act 2013, **companies with a share capital structure** must obtain the Commencement of Business (COB) Certificate before commencing business operations. This requirement is applicable to:

**Companies Incorporated After November 2, 2018**: All companies registered after this date must obtain the COB Certificate within 180 days of their incorporation.

**Companies with Share Capita** l: Every company operating with a share capital structure, irrespective of business type, must apply for the COB Certificate.

**Includes:**

- Private Limited Companies
- Public Limited Companies
- Section 8 Companies (with share capital structure)

## Significance of the Certificate of Commencement of Business

The Commencement of Business Certificate holds considerable significance as it officially indicates a company’s readiness to begin operations.

- **Operational Readiness Confirmation:** This commencement of buinesscertificate serves as proof that the company has met all the legal prerequisites and is fully prepared to engage in business activities.
- **Legitimacy Assurance:** It assures stakeholders, investors, and regulatory authorities that the company is operating in accordance with established regulations, thereby reinforcing its legitimacy and accountability.

## Due Date for Obtaining the Certificate of Commencement of Business (COB)

All companies with a share capital structure must obtain the Commencement of Business Certificate within **180 days of their incorporation**. Adhering to this deadline is essential to avoid penalties and potential disqualification.

## Commencement of business Form 20A Filing Exemptions

Specific categories of companies are exempt from filing Form 20A, including:

- **Companies Incorporated Before November 2, 2018:** All companies formed prior to this date are exempt from filing the form.
- **Companies Without Share Capital:** Businesses that operate without a share capital structure do not need to submit Form 20A.

## Consequences of Non-Compliance with Commencement of Business (COB)

Failure to file the Commencement of Business Certificate (COB) within the prescribed 180-day period can have severe repercussions:

- **Prohibition on Business Operations:** The company will be prohibited from commencing its business activities or accessing any borrowing facilities.
- **Penalties on the Company:** The company will incur a penalty of Rs. 50,000.
- **Penalties on Directors:** Each defaulting director will face a penalty of Rs. 1,000 per day, up to a maximum of Rs. 1,00,000.
- **Potential Strike-Off:** If no declaration is filed, and the Registrar of Companies (RoC) has reasonable grounds to believe the company is not conducting business or operations, the RoC may initiate action to remove the company’s name from its register, resulting in a company strike-off.

## Documents Required for Filing Form 20A

To successfully file the Commencement of Business Form 20A, the following documents are required:

- **Proof of Payment for Share Subscription:** Bank statement showing receipt of subscription money from the subscribers.
- **Registered Office Address Verification:** Evidence of the company’s registered office address.
- **Certificate of Registration from RBI (if applicable):** Mandatory for Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) or entities regulated by other financial authorities.
- **Directors’ Declaration and Board Resolution:** Declaration by the directors affirming that the subscribers have paid the share value, along with a supporting board resolution.

## Procedure for Obtaining the Certificate of Commencement of Business

Follow these steps to obtain the certificate of commencement of business mca by filing Form 20A:

- **Access the MCA Portal:** Log in to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) portal with your credentials.
- **Download Form 20A:** Go to “MCA Services” and select “Company Forms Download.” Choose Form 20A (Declaration of Commencement of Business).
- **Complete the Form:** Enter the necessary company details such as the Corporate Identification Number (CIN) and other information.
- **Attach Required Documents:** Attach the proof of payment for the shared subscription, the registered office address verification, and any applicable documents like the RBI registration certificate.
- **Affix the Digital Signature Certificate (DSC):** Ensure the form is signed using the Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) of an authorised director.
- **Professional Certification:** The commencement of business form must be verified and certified by a Chartered Accountant (CA), Company Secretary (CS), or Cost Accountant (CWA).
- **Submit the Form and Pay Fees:** Submit Form 20A along with the required attachments through the MCA portal. Pay the applicable fees based on the company’s share capital.
- **Verification and Acknowledgment:** Once submitted, a Service Request Number (SRN) will be generated. Upon verification, an acknowledgement email will be sent confirming the successful filing of Form 20A.

# DIR 3 KYC - Application for KYC of Directors

A [Director Identification Number (DIN)](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/complete-guide-on-director-identification-number-din) is a unique number assigned to an individual who wishes to become a director or is already serving as a director of a company. Earlier, obtaining a DIN was a one-time process that required submitting an application through e-Form DIR-3.

However, with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) now updating its records, every director holding a DIN must annually submit their [KYC details](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/know-your-customer-kyc) by filing e-Form DIR-3 KYC.

If you're a director needing to fulfill annual KYC requirements, IndiaFilings makes it simple and hassle-free. Our experts are ready to assist you with your DIR 3 KYC filing to ensure you remain compliant with MCA regulations.

Complete Your DIR 3 KYC Filing Effortlessly with IndiaFilings!

## What is  DIR-3 KYC Form?

As mentioned, Form DIR-3 KYC is an electronic form mandated by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) for the purpose of updating the KYC (Know Your Customer) details of individuals who have been allotted a Director Identification Number (DIN).

## Applicability of MCA Form DIR 3KYC

Form DIR-3 KYC is a mandatory filing requirement under the Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014. It applies to individuals who have been allotted a Director Identification Number (DIN) and whose DIN status is 'approved'.

### Purpose of DIN KYC  Filing

The purpose of this form is to conduct the annual KYC (Know Your Customer) process for directors, which must be submitted to the Registrar of Companies (ROC). This form is essential for maintaining current and accurate director information with the ROC, including addresses, contact numbers, and email addresses.

## DIR-3 KYC Due Date

According to the recent announcement by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA), every director who was allotted a DIN on or before 31st March 2018 and whose DIN is in approved status must submit their KYC details to the MCA. This requirement also applies to disqualified directors.

From the Financial Year 2019–20 onwards, it is mandatory for every director who has been allotted a DIN on or before the end of the financial year and whose DIN remains approved to file Form DIR-3 KYC by 30th September of the immediately following financial year.

Latest Update: For the Financial Year 2024–25, the last date for filing DIR-3 KYC without a fee has been extended to 31st October 2025 from the earlier due date of 15 October 2025 . After this date, a late filing fee of ₹500 will be applicable.

## Types of e-Form DIR-3 KYC

Directors must submit their KYC details each year, and the Ministry of Corporate Affairs offers two ways to do this. The type of form to be filed depends on whether it is the first submission or if any changes in details are required.

DIR-3 KYC (Form)

- To be filed for the first time after a DIN is allotted.
- Also required if there is any change or update in the director’s KYC details, such as a new mobile number or email address.

### DIR 3 KYC WEB

- To be filed by a director who has already submitted DIR-3 KYC or DIR-3 KYC (Web) in a previous year, provided there is no change in KYC details.
- In this version, the director’s basic information is pre-filled from the MCA database and cannot be edited.

## Checkpoints for Filing e-Form DIR-3 KYC

When submitting the e-Form DIR-3 KYC, directors should keep the following points in mind:

- Personal Contact Details: Provide your own mobile number and email address. These will be verified through a one-time password (OTP).
- Digital Signature: The form must be signed using the director’s own [digital signature](https://www.indiafilings.com/digital-signature).
- Accuracy and Certification: Ensure that all details entered are complete and accurate. The form must be certified by a practising Chartered Accountant (CA), Company Secretary (CS), or Cost Accountant.

## Consequences of Not Filing e-Form DIR-3 KYC Within the Due Date

If a director fails to file the e-Form DIR-3 KYC on the MCA21 portal by 30th September, the Director Identification Number (DIN) will be marked as “Deactivated due to Non-filing of DIR-3 KYC” by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

To [reactivate the DIN](https://www.indiafilings.com/din-reactivation) in the future, the director must file the pending e-Form DIR-3 KYC and pay a late fee of ₹5,000. This penalty applies on or after 30th September of the relevant year. Filing the e-Form DIR-3 KYC is an annual requirement for all directors.

## Documents Required for Filing e-Form DIR-3 KYC

To file the DIR-3 KYC form, keep the following documents ready:

- Permanent address proof – such as Voter ID, Driving Licence, or PAN card.
- Present address proof – for example, a recent utility bill (not older than 2 months) or a rental agreement.
- Aadhaar card.
- Passport.
- Other supporting documents (if applicable).

In addition to the above, ensure you have:

- The Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) of the director (applicant) filing the form.
- The DSC, membership number, and certificate of practice number of a practising professional, such as a Chartered Accountant (CA), Company Secretary (CS), or Cost Accountant.

## How to File DIR 3 KYC: Step-by-Step Guide

Here is a detailed guide to help you complete the filing of e-Form DIR-3 KYC successfully:

### Step 1: Log in to the MCA Website

Start by visiting the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) website. On the homepage, click on the ‘Sign In/Sign Up’ button.

- If you are an existing user, log in directly by entering your User ID and password.
- If you are a new user and have not yet registered on the MCA website, click the ‘Register’ button. Provide all the required details in the registration form and create your account. Once registered, you can log in using the User ID and password created during registration.

### Step 2: Provide Mobile Number and Email for OTP Verification

- After logging in to the MCA website, go to the ‘MCA Services’ tab. From there, navigate to ‘Company e-Filing’, then select ‘DIN Related Filings’ and click on ‘Form DIR-3 KYC’ or ‘Form DIR-3 KYC Web’.
- On the form, the director needs to enter the DIN number, mobile number, and email address.
- An OTP (One-Time Password) will be sent to both the registered mobile number and email address.
- Enter the OTPs received on both mediums and then click on ‘Next’ to proceed.

### Step 3: Enter Personal and Identification Details in the MCA DIR 3 KYC form

On the next page of the form, the director must fill in the following details accurately:

- Full Name
- Father’s name
- Nationality
- Date of birth
- Gender
- PAN number (Permanent Account Number)
- Mobile number and the OTP sent to the mobile number
- Email ID and the OTP sent to the email ID
- Aadhaar number
- Permanent residential addresses
- Present residential address

If the director is filing the e-Form DIR-3 KYC (Web), most of the above details will already be pre-filled from the MCA database. Only the details that are not pre-filled will need to be entered by the director.

Important Note: It is mandatory to declare your [Permanent Account Number (PAN](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/pan-permanent-account-number)). After entering the PAN details, click on the ‘Verify income-tax PAN’ button. The system will automatically verify the information based on the PAN card number. In the case of foreign nationals who do not possess a PAN, the name entered in the form must exactly match the name provided in the Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) to ensure successful validation.

### Step 4: Upload Attachments and Certify the e-Form

Once all details are entered, the director must upload the required documents. After attaching the necessary documents, the director must make a declaration confirming that the information provided in the e-Form DIR-3 KYC is true and correct.

- Attach the director’s own Digital Signature Certificate (DSC).
-  The e-Form must also be digitally signed by a practising professional, which can be a Chartered Accountant (CA), a Company Secretary (CS), or a Cost Accountant.
- Enter the professional’s membership number and other details, and attach the digital signature of the professional certifying the form.

Finally, after completing these steps, click the ‘Submit’ button to submit the DIR-3 KYC form successfully.

### Service Request Number (SRN) Generation

Upon successful submission of the e-Form DIR-3 KYC, a Service Request Number (SRN) will be generated automatically. This SRN acts as a unique reference and should be carefully saved for any future correspondence or communication with the MCA.

### Email Communication and Confirmation

An official email confirming the approval and receipt of the form will be sent to the personal email ID of the applicant. Once this confirmation email is received, it serves as proof that the process of filing the e-Form DIR-3 KYC has been successfully completed.

## File Your DIR-3 KYC Easily with IndiaFilings!

Looking to complete your DIR-3 KYC filing quickly and hassle-free? Let IndiaFilings handle the process for you. Our team of experts will guide you through every step from preparing the required documents to submitting the form, ensuring 100% compliance with MCA regulations. Save time, avoid penalties, and stay updated with the latest legal requirements.

# Form DPT-3 Return Filing

Every company, excluding government companies, must file a return of deposits in Form DPT-3 with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) by June 30th each year. This return should include details of deposits, outstanding loans, and any amounts received that do not qualify as deposits as of March 31st of that year. DPT-3 return is audited by the company's auditor to ensure accuracy and compliance.

_**IndiaFilings experts can assist you in filing your DPT-3 form accurately and efficiently. Get started today and simplify your compliance process!**_

## Introduction to DPT-3 Filing

To safeguard the interests of creditors and depositors, the Central Government, in consultation with the Reserve Bank
of India, introduced an amendment to the Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules 2014 through the Companies
(Acceptance of Deposits) Amendment Rules 2019.

In line with this, MCA, vide its notification dated 22nd January 2019, notified that every company other than a
government company must file a one-time return in DPT 3. It is also required to be filed annually. Accordingly, a
sub-rule (3) was inserted after sub-rule (2) in Rule 16A of the Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules, 2014,
which reads as follows:

_Every company other than Government company shall file a onetime return of outstanding receipt of money or loan by_
_a company but not considered as deposits, in terms of clause (c) of sub-rule 1 of rule 2 from the 01st April,_
_2014 to 31st March, 2019, as specified in Form DPT-3 within ninety days from 31st March, 2019 along with a fee_
_as provided in the Companies (Registration Offices and Fees) Rules, 2014._

## Eligible Companies for Form DPT-3 Return Filing

Form DPT-3, filing the return of deposits, applies to several types of companies in India. The following categories
of companies are eligible to file Form DPT-3:

- Private Limited Companies
- Public Limited Companies
- One Person Companies (OPC)
- Small and Non-Small Companies

It is important to note that even if a company has received a loan from specific entities, it must file Form DPT-3.
These entities include:

- **Holding Company:** If a company has obtained a loan from its holding company, which has a
controlling stake, Form DPT-3 filing is mandatory.
- **Subsidiary Company:** In the case of a loan from a subsidiary company controlled by the borrowing
company, filing Form DPT-3 is necessary.
- **Associate Company:** When a company has received a loan from an associate company with a
significant influence on the borrowing entity, filing Form DPT-3 is obligatory.

It is important to note that government companies are exempted from filing Form DPT-3.

## Exempted Companies from Filing Form DPT-3

Under the Acceptance of Deposits Rules of 2014, certain companies are exempted from filing the DPT-3 form as per the
Companies Act. The exemptions primarily relate to the filing of loan returns. The following types of companies are
exempt from filing Form DPT-3:

- **Government Companies:** Companies wholly owned and controlled by the Central or State Government
are exempt from filing DPT-3.
- **Specified Financial Institutions:** Certain financial institutions are exempt due to their
existing regulatory framework. This includes:
- **Banking Companies:**Banks regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) are not required to file
DPT-3.
  - Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs): NBFCs registered with the RBI are exempt.
  - Housing Finance Companies: Companies registered as housing finance companies under the National Housing
     Bank (NHB) do not need to file DPT-3.
- **Other Notified Companies:** In rare cases, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) might notify
specific companies under a special provision (proviso to subsection (1) of section 73 of the Act) for exemption
from DPT-3 filing.

## Form DPT-3 Applicability

All companies, except those mentioned under exemptions, are required to file the DPT-3 return if they have received
the following:

- Deposits from members or directors
- Loans from third parties
- Advances for goods or services (secured or unsecured)

The filing of Form DPT-3 applies to a wide range of monetary transactions and debts. Here are the types of money or
debts to which Form DPT-3 is applicable:

- **Secured Debts:** These are loans or obligations backed by collateral or security the borrowing
company provides.
- **Unsecured Debts:** These are loans or debts without collateral or security attached.
- **External Borrowings:** Form DPT-3 also encompasses debts or borrowings from external sources,
such as financial institutions or banks.
- **Commercial Borrowings:** Loans or debts obtained by companies for commercial purposes are covered
by Form DPT-3.

## Transactions Not Considered as Deposits for DPT-3 Filing

Form DPT-3 focuses on reporting deposits a company receives. Here is what doesn't count as a deposit:

- **Share Capital:** Money received from shareholders for shares.
- **Debentures Issued:** Loans from investors, treated separately.
- **Advances on Orders:** Payments are received upfront for confirmed orders.
- **Government Receipts:** Money from government or foreign sources.
- **Loans from Banks**: Money borrowed from banks or financial institutions.
- **Inter-Company Loans:** Loans from other companies.
- **Subscription Advances:** Money paid in advance for upcoming securities.
- **Employee Deposits:** Security deposits from employees up to their annual salary.

## Form DPT 3 Due Date

**The due date for filing Form DPT 3 is June 30th of every year.** This deadline applies to all
companies required to report their deposits or outstanding receipts of loans or money not considered deposits for
the financial year ending on March 31st.

Here's a breakdown for clarity:

- **Financial Year:** The financial year in India typically runs from April 1st to March 31st of the
following year.
- **DPT-3 Reporting:** Companies must report all deposits and outstanding receipts that occurred
during this financial year.
- **Due Date:** The deadline to file DPT-3 for the previous financial year falls on June 30th.

Example: **For the financial year 2023-24 (April 1, 2023, to March 31, 2024), the DPT-3 filing deadline would**
**be June 30, 2024.**

## Documents Required for Filing Form DPT-3:

To complete the filing of Form DPT-3, the following documents are typically required:

- **Auditor's Certificate:** An auditor's certificate verifying the information provided in the DPT-3
form regarding the company's deposits and outstanding receipts is mandatory.

Optional Documents (depending on your specific situation):

- **Proof of Trust Deed:** If your company has created a trust to hold deposits received, a
copy of the trust deed needs to be attached.
- **Instrument Creating Charge (if any):** In case your company has created a charge (security
interest) on any assets to secure deposits, a copy of the instrument creating that charge must be uploaded.
- **Details of Liquid Assets:** The DPT-3 filing may require information on the company's liquid
assets, which are assets that can be easily converted into cash. Documents supporting these details may be
required.
- **List of Depositors (in some cases):**  Depending on the specific type and value of deposits
received, the MCA might require a list of depositors with their details.

## Fees for Filing Form DPT-3

The fees for filing Form DPT-3 are determined as per the Companies (Registration Offices and Fees) Rules.

## Consequences of Non-compliance with the DPT-3 filing

Non-compliance with the DPT-3 filing requirement pursuant to Rules 16 and 16A of the Companies (Acceptance of
Deposits) Rules, 2014. can lead to penalties and other legal consequences. Therefore, it is in the best interest of
companies to diligently complete and submit the form to the MCA within the stipulated timeframe. By doing so,
companies can maintain good standing with regulatory authorities and ensure that their financial activities are in
accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

## DPT-3 Penalty

According to the Companies Act 2013, if a company or any of its officers fail to comply with the filing requirement
of Form DPT-3 or commit any default related to the filing, they can be subjected to penalties-

- **Fine for the Company:** The company itself can be fined an amount that may extend up to five
thousand rupees.
- **Fine for Officers in Default:** The officers of the company who are responsible for the default
can also be fined an amount that may extend up to five thousand rupees.
- **Additional Fine for Continuing Contravention:** If the contravention or default is a continuing
one, i.e., it persists beyond the first day, then a further fine may be imposed. This additional fine can be up
to five hundred rupees for each day after the first day, during which the contravention continues.

These penalties are intended to ensure compliance with the filing requirements and regulations under the Companies
Act 2013. For companies and their officers to fulfil their obligations, including the timely and accurate filing of
Form DPT-3, to avoid such penalties and maintain compliance with the law.

## How to File DPT-3?

Form DPT-3 is a web-based form that must be filed online through the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) website. The
process involves several steps, which are outlined below to give you a comprehensive understanding of the DPT 3
filing procedure. If you encounter any issues or need professional assistance, our experts are always available to
help.

### Visit the MCA Portal & Login:

- Go to the MCA website. This is the official portal for all e-filing and services provided by the Ministry of
Corporate Affairs, including the filing of Form DPT-3.
- Log into your account. If you do not have an account, you can create one by registering as a Business User.

### Access the DPT-3 Webform:

- Navigate to the Form: Once logged in, go to the main menu, and under the  MCA Services section, click on
    e-filing services.
- Select Deposit Filings: From the dropdown menu, select  Deposit Related Filings and then access the DPT-3
Webform. The entire process is conducted online from start to finish.

### Fill Out & Submit the Form Online:

Here is the information to be furnished when filing Form DPT-3:

- **CIN of the Company:** The Corporate Identification Number (CIN) assigned to the company.
- **Email ID:** The official email address of the company for communication purposes.
- **Objects of the Company:** A description of the primary business activities or purposes for which
the company was established.
- **Net Worth of the Company:** The net worth of the company as of the most recent financial
year-end, typically calculated as total assets minus total liabilities.
- **Particulars of Charge (if any):** Details of any charges or encumbrances on the company's assets.

- **Total Amount Outstanding as of 31st March 2020:** The total outstanding amount of deposits,
loans, or other funds as of March 31st, 2020.
- **Particulars of Credit Rating:** Information on the credit rating of the company, if applicable,
including the name of the credit rating agency and the rating assigned.
- **Attachments:** Attach the necessary documents in digital format to support the details provided
in the form. A comprehensive list of required documents is provided in the section above.

### Submit the Form to Generate SRN:

- **Form Submission:** After filling out the form and attaching the required documents, submit the
form online. A Service Request Number (SRN) will be generated, which you can use to track the status of your
form until all formalities are completed.

### Affix the DSC & Pay the Required Fee:

- **Digital Signature:** Authenticate the form with the applicant's Digital Signature Certificate
(DSC).
- **Fee Payment:** Pay the required fee for the DPT-3 filing. The fee varies based on the company's
nominal or paid-up capital and increases accordingly. Detailed fee structures are provided in the further
sections.

### Receive the acknowledgement mail:

- **Acknowledgement:** You will receive an acknowledgement of your filing on your registered email
address, confirming that the Registrar of Companies has received the return of deposits for the financial year.

Completing the DPT-3 filing process is essential for regulatory compliance and avoiding penalties. Contact our
experts to ensure a smooth and efficient filing experience if you need further guidance or support.
