services.content:
## 15CA - 15CB Filing

Form 15CA and Form 15CB filing is mandatory for making payments to non-residents under the Income Tax Act. We assist with tax determination, DTAA benefit analysis, CA certification, and online filing to ensure hassle-free foreign remittance compliance.

## File Your 15CA - 15CB

Easily file Form 15CA and obtain Form 15CB certificate from a Chartered Accountant for foreign remittances. Ensure proper tax compliance and smooth processing of international payments.

- CA Certificate (Form 15CB) Preparation
- Online Filing of Form 15CA
- Quick Processing for Foreign Remittance
- DTAA & TDS Compliance Verification

# 15CA and 15CB Filing Online for Foreign Remittances in India

**Form 15CA** and **Form 15CB** are mandatory compliance documents required for **foreign remittances from India**. Any person making a payment to a non-resident must submit these forms on the **income tax e-filing portal** before initiating the transfer to ensure full compliance with the Income Tax Act, 1961 and FEMA regulations governing **cross-border payments from India**.

For seamless [income tax filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax-filing) and complete foreign remittance compliance support, IndiaFilings provides end-to-end expert assistance from start to finish.

## What is Form 15CA and Form 15CB?

**Form 15CA** and **Form 15CB** are two distinct but interrelated **foreign remittance compliance India** documents mandated under Section 195 of the Income Tax Act, 1961. Every remitter making a **cross-border payment to a non-resident** must understand the nature, purpose, and applicability of both forms before initiating any outward foreign transfer. Ensuring complete [income tax compliance India](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax) is the first step before making any remittance abroad.

### What is Form 15CA?

**Form 15CA** is a **self-declaration form** submitted by the remitter (payer) to the Income Tax Department before making a payment to a non-resident or foreign company. It is an undertaking confirming that applicable taxes have been deducted or that the remittance is exempt from tax. The form is filed online on the **income tax e-filing portal** and is mandatory for most **cross-border payments from India**.

### What is Form 15CB?

**Form 15CB** is a **certificate issued by a [Chartered Accountant](https://www.indiafilings.com/chartered-accountant-services) (CA)** certifying the nature and taxability of the remittance. The CA verifies the applicable **[Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/guide-to-double-taxation-treaty-in-india) (DTAA)** provisions, the rate of TDS, and the nature of the payment before issuing this certificate. **Form 15CB** must be obtained before filing **Part C of Form 15CA** for remittances above Rs. 5 lakh in a financial year.

### Difference Between Form 15CA and Form 15CB

| Feature | Form 15CA | Form 15CB |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nature | Self-declaration by remitter | Certificate issued by Chartered Accountant |
| Filed By | Remitter (Payer) | Chartered Accountant |
| Purpose | Declaration of taxability of foreign remittance | Certification of nature and tax liability |
| Filed On | Income Tax e-Filing Portal | Income Tax e-Filing Portal |
| When Required | For most foreign remittances | Required for Part C of Form 15CA |
| Applicable Amount | All taxable remittances | Remittances above Rs. 5 lakh per year |

## What are the Types of Form 15CA?

Form 15CA is divided into **four parts (Part A, B, C, and D)** based on the nature and amount of remittance. Each part has different applicability and filing requirements under **Rule 37BB of the Income Tax Rules**. Businesses and professionals who are also required to file their annual returns should ensure their [business tax return filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-itr-filing) accurately reflects all foreign remittances made during the financial year.

### Part A – Remittance Below Rs. 5 Lakh

**Part A** of Form 15CA is applicable when the **remittance is below Rs. 5 lakh** in a financial year and the payment is taxable under the Income Tax Act. In this case, **Form 15CB is not required** and the remitter can file directly on the portal after self-assessment of tax liability.

### Part B – Remittance with Tax Determination Order

**Part B** is applicable when the remitter has obtained a **certificate or order from the Assessing Officer** under Section 195(2), 195(3), or 197 of the Income Tax Act. The details of the order must be mentioned in Part B and **Form 15CB is not required** in this case.

### Part C – Remittance Above Rs. 5 Lakh

**Part C** is the most commonly used part and is applicable when the **remittance exceeds Rs. 5 lakh** in a financial year and the payment is taxable. In this case, **Form 15CB from a Chartered Accountant is mandatory** before filing Part C of Form 15CA.

### Part D – Remittances Not Chargeable to Tax

**Part D** is applicable when the remittance is **not chargeable to tax in India** under the Income Tax Act or under the applicable DTAA. In such cases, neither Form 15CB nor any tax deduction is required, but the remitter must still file Part D of Form 15CA.

## What are the Key Details for 15CA & 15CB Filing?

The following overview table covers all essential details about **15CA 15CB filing online in India** that remitters and businesses must know before initiating a foreign payment. Before filing these forms, entities must ensure they hold a valid [TAN registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/tan-registration) as TDS deduction and deposit on foreign payments is mandatory under the Income Tax Act.

| Category | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Form Type | Form 15CA (Remitter) and Form 15CB (Chartered Accountant) |
| Applicable To | Individuals, firms, companies making payments to non-residents |
| Filed On | Income Tax e-Filing Portal – incometax.gov.in |
| Governing Law | Section 195 of Income Tax Act, Rule 37BB of Income Tax Rules |
| Form 15CB Requirement | Mandatory for taxable remittances above Rs. 5 lakh (Part C) |
| Mode of Filing | Online – Mandatory |
| Penalty for Non-Filing | Rs. 1 lakh under Section 271-I |
| DTAA Benefit | Available if applicable treaty provisions are cited |

## What is the Applicability of Form 15CA and Form 15CB?

**Form 15CA and Form 15CB** are applicable to all persons – individuals, firms, and companies – who make payments to **non-residents or foreign companies** that are chargeable to tax in India. The **TDS deduction on foreign remittance** must be completed and reported accurately. Businesses that deduct TDS on foreign payments must also ensure timely [TDS return filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/tds-return-filing) to avoid interest and penalties under the Income Tax Act.

### When is Form 15CA Applicable?

- Payment made to a **non-resident or foreign company**
- Payment is **chargeable to tax** in India under the Income Tax Act
- Payment is made for services, royalties, dividends, interest, or other income
- Remittance processed through **authorised dealers or banks** in India
- Both **taxable and non-taxable remittances** – Part D applies for non-taxable payments

### When is Form 15CB Applicable?

- When the remittance exceeds **Rs. 5 lakh in a financial year**
- When the payment is **taxable in India** under the Income Tax Act
- When **Part C of Form 15CA** is being filed by the remitter
- CA must certify the **applicable tax rate, DTAA provisions**, and nature of income

## When is Form 15CA Not Required?

Not all foreign remittances require the filing of **Form 15CA**. Under **Rule 37BB of the Income Tax Rules**, certain specified payments are completely exempt from this filing requirement. Individual business owners and proprietors making foreign remittances should also ensure their annual income is correctly disclosed by filing [ITR 3 Form](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-3-form) to avoid any tax discrepancies.

### Exempted Payments Under Rule 37BB

| Sr. No. | Nature of Remittance Exempted |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Indian investment abroad – in equity capital or debt securities |
| 2 | Payments for imports of goods into India |
| 3 | Remittance by a non-resident out of funds received in India |
| 4 | Payments by diplomatic missions and their employees |
| 5 | Remittances for shipping and air freight charges |
| 6 | Personal gifts or donations below specified limits |
| 7 | Payments under approved education loans and tuition fees abroad |
| 8 | Payments for medical treatment abroad |
| 9 | Travel-related remittances including business travel expenses |
| 10 | Remittances covered under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) for personal use |

## When is Form 15CB Not Required?

**Form 15CB** is not required in the following specific scenarios. Understanding these conditions helps the remitter determine whether a **Chartered Accountant certificate for foreign remittance** is mandatory before initiating the outward payment. Partnership firms and LLPs making foreign payments should also file their [ITR 5 Form](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-5-form) accurately to reflect all cross-border transactions in their annual income tax return.

### Conditions When Form 15CB is Not Needed

- When the remittance is **below Rs. 5 lakh** in a financial year – Part A of Form 15CA applies
- When the remitter has obtained a **certificate or order from the Assessing Officer** under Section 195(2), 195(3), or 197 – Part B of Form 15CA applies
- When the remittance is **not chargeable to tax** in India – Part D of Form 15CA applies
- When the payment falls under the **list of exempted remittances under Rule 37BB**
- When the remittance is covered under a **specific DTAA exemption** that eliminates Indian tax liability

## Who is Required to File Form 15CA and 15CB?

Any **person making a payment to a non-resident** that is chargeable to tax in India is required to file Form 15CA before the remittance is processed. Companies that make foreign payments must also ensure their corporate tax returns are filed correctly by using [ITR 6 Form](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-6-form) to disclose all outward foreign remittances made during the financial year.

### Who Must File Form 15CA?

- **Individuals** making payments to non-residents for services, royalties, or other income
- **Companies and firms** remitting money abroad for business purposes
- **[Partnership firms](https://www.indiafilings.com/partnership) and [LLPs](https://www.indiafilings.com/llp-registration)** making cross-border payments to foreign parties
- **[Trusts](https://www.indiafilings.com/trust-registration) and [NGOs](https://www.indiafilings.com/producer-company-registration)** transferring funds abroad for permitted purposes
- Any person making payment under **Section 195 of the Income Tax Act**

### When Do You Need Form 15CB?

- When filing **Part C of Form 15CA** for remittances above Rs. 5 lakh
- When the remittance is taxable and no **Assessing Officer order** has been obtained
- When the CA needs to certify the **applicable DTAA provisions** and rate of tax
- Before the bank processes the **outward wire transfer** above Rs. 5 lakh

## What is the Mandatory Information Required for Form 15CA and 15CB Filing?

Having all the required information ready ensures a smooth and accurate **15CA 15CB online submission process**. Providing complete and correct details avoids rejection and delays in processing the **foreign remittance tax compliance** requirements under the Income Tax Act, 1961.

### Information Required for Form 15CA

- PAN and TAN of the remitter
- Name and address of the **non-resident recipient**
- Country of remittance and **currency of payment**
- Amount of remittance in Indian Rupees and foreign currency
- Nature of payment – royalty, interest, dividend, fees for technical services, etc.
- Applicable **DTAA article** and rate of tax if DTAA benefit is being claimed
- Bank details for the remittance transaction
- **Form 15CB acknowledgement number** – required for Part C filing

### Information Required for Form 15CB (by CA)

- Details of the **remitter and recipient** including PAN and address
- Nature and purpose of the remittance
- Applicable **DTAA provisions** and certified tax rate
- Amount of TDS deducted and deposited with challan details
- CA membership number and digital signature certificate
- **Tax Residency Certificate** of the non-resident if DTAA benefit is claimed

## What Documents are Required for 15CA and 15CB Filing?

The following documents are required to file **Form 15CA** and obtain **Form 15CB** from a Chartered Accountant. Having all documents ready in advance ensures faster processing of **foreign remittance compliance India** requirements without delays at the bank or authorised dealer level.

### Documents Required for Form 15CA

- [PAN card](https://www.indiafilings.com/pan-card) and [TAN](https://www.indiafilings.com/tan-registration) of the remitter
- Invoice or agreement with the foreign party
- Bank account details for the remittance
- Form 15CB acknowledgement number for Part C
- Assessing Officer order under Section 195(2), 195(3), or 197 for Part B
- DTAA certificate or tax residency certificate if applicable

### Documents Required for Form 15CB

- PAN and TAN of the remitter
- Invoice or contract for the foreign payment
- **Tax Residency Certificate (TRC)** of the non-resident
- Form 10F from the non-resident if applicable
- Bank remittance details and purpose code
- Proof of TDS deduction and challan payment
- Financial statements of the non-resident entity if required by CA

## How to File Form 15CA and 15CB Online?

The **Form 15CA and 15CB filing process** is entirely online through the **income tax e-filing portal – incometax.gov.in**. Both the remitter and the Chartered Accountant must be registered on the portal with valid login credentials before initiating the **15CA 15CB online filing procedure**.

### Step-by-Step Guide to File Form 15CB Online

1. The Chartered Accountant logs in to **incometax.gov.in** using CA credentials
2. Navigate to e-File, then Income Tax Forms, then File Income Tax Forms
3. Select **Form 15CB** from the dropdown list
4. Fill in all details – remitter, recipient, nature of payment, applicable tax rate, and DTAA provisions
5. Verify and submit using the CA's **[Digital Signature Certificate](https://www.indiafilings.com/digital-signature)(DSC)**
6. Note the **Form 15CB Acknowledgement Number** for use in Form 15CA Part C

### Step-by-Step Guide to File Form 15CA Online

1. Log in to **incometax.gov.in** using the remitter's PAN and registered password
2. Navigate to e-File, then Income Tax Forms, then File Income Tax Forms
3. Select **Form 15CA** from the list
4. Choose the applicable **Part – A, B, C, or D** based on the nature and amount of remittance
5. Fill in all required details including the **Form 15CB acknowledgement number** for Part C
6. Preview and verify all entered information carefully
7. Submit the form using **e-Verify via [Aadhaar](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/eaadhaar-download) OTP, Net Banking, or DSC**
8. Download the **acknowledgement slip** and submit to the bank to process the remittance

## What is the Timeline for 15CA and 15CB Filing?

The **15CA 15CB filing timeline** must be carefully followed to avoid delays in processing the **outward remittance India tax** compliance. Entities that have submitted incorrect details in any previous return can file a [revised return](https://www.indiafilings.com/revised-return) to correct errors before the applicable deadline to avoid penalties.

### 15CA 15CB Filing Timeline

| Step | Activity | Timeline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Step 1 | Obtain Form 15CB from Chartered Accountant | Before filing Form 15CA Part C |
| Step 2 | File Form 15CA on income tax e-filing portal | Before initiating the remittance |
| Step 3 | Submit acknowledgement to the bank or authorised dealer | At the time of remittance |
| Step 4 | Bank processes outward remittance | After verification of all submitted documents |
| Step 5 | Disclose foreign remittance in annual income tax return | At the time of filing annual ITR |

## What are the Consequences of Non-Compliance in 15CA 15CB Filing?

Failure to comply with **Form 15CA and 15CB filing requirements** can result in severe penalties and legal consequences under the Income Tax Act, 1961. Taxpayers who receive an [income tax notice](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax-notice) for non-compliance or incorrect filing must respond promptly with all required supporting documentation to avoid further escalation.

### Penalties and Consequences Table

| Type of Non-Compliance | Penalty or Consequence |
| --- | --- |
| Non-filing of Form 15CA | Penalty of Rs. 1 lakh under Section 271-I |
| Filing incorrect information in Form 15CA | Penalty of Rs. 1 lakh under Section 271-I |
| Non-deduction of TDS on foreign payment | Disallowance of expense under Section 40(a)(i) |
| Short deduction of TDS on remittance | Interest under Section 201(1A) at 1.5% per month |
| Bank processing remittance without Form 15CA | Liable under Section 195(6) for non-compliance |
| Non-filing of Form 15CB by CA | Disciplinary action by ICAI and income tax department scrutiny |

## Why Should You Choose IndiaFilings for 15CA 15CB Filing Services?

IndiaFilings is a trusted platform for **15CA 15CB filing online in India**, offering end-to-end expert assistance for businesses and individuals making foreign remittances. Our qualified Chartered Accountants handle **Form 15CB certification**, Form 15CA filing, and complete **foreign remittance tax compliance** with speed and accuracy. Whether you are a company, partnership firm, or individual remitter, IndiaFilings ensures your foreign payment is fully compliant with all income tax requirements.

## Frequently asked questions

Common questions aboutForm 15CA-15CB Filing Online India.

What is Form 15CA-15CB?

Form 15CA is a declaration form that must be submitted electronically by the remitter to the bank before paying a non-resident. Form 15CB is a certificate issued by a Chartered Accountant (CA) to verify the deduction of taxes and the completion of other regulatory requirements.

What is the difference between Form 15CA and Form 15CB?

Form 15CA is a declaration form submitted by the remitter to the bank. At the same time, Form 15CB is a certificate issued by a CA to verify the deduction of taxes and the completion of other regulatory requirements.

Who is required to file Form 15CA-15CB?

Form 15CA and 15CB must be filed by a person responsible for remittance outside India. The remitter can be an individual, a company, or any other entity paying a non-resident or a foreign company.

What are the different types of transactions that require 15CA-15CB filing?

Different types of transactions require Form 15CA and 15CB filing. Some of them are:

- Payment for import of goods or services.
- Payment for royalty or technical fees.
- Remittance of dividends.
- Payment for interest on loans or deposits.
- Payment for foreign collaborations or joint ventures.
- Remittance for education-related expenses.
- Remittance for medical treatment abroad.
- Remittance for travel expenses.
- Remittance for payment of insurance premium.
- Any other taxable payment or remittance under the Income Tax Act, 1961.

Is Form 15CA-15CB mandatory for all foreign remittances?

Form 15CA and 15CB are not mandatory for all foreign remittances. The requirement to file these forms depends on the nature and amount of the remittance.

As per the current regulations, Form 15CA and 15CB are mandatory for remittances made outside India, except for the following:

- Remittances are covered under specified exemptions as per Rule 37BB of the Income Tax Rules, 1962. Some examples of exempted remittances include gifts and donations, payments made by the Government, payments for certain investments, etc.
- Remittances below INR 5 lakhs are not subject to TDS under Section 195 of the Income Tax Act, 1961.

How is the information provided in Form 15CA verified?

The information provided in Form 15CA is verified by the Authorized Dealer Bank (AD Bank) and is cross-checked with the information in Form 15CB.

Can Form 15CA-15CB be filed manually?

Form 15CA-15CB must be filed electronically through the Income Tax Department's website.

What is the penalty for not filing Form 15CA-15CB?

Non-compliance with the requirement to file Form 15CA and 15CB can attract penalties and interest. The penalty for not filing Form 15CA and 15CB is covered under Section 271-I of the Income Tax Act, 1961. As per the current regulations, the penalty for non-filing or incorrect filing of Form 15CA and 15CB is INR 1 lakh or equal to the transaction amount, whichever is lower. The penalty can be imposed by the Assessing Officer (AO) after providing an opportunity for the remitter to explain the reasons for non-compliance.

Can the same Form 15CA be used for multiple transactions?

No, the same Form 15CA cannot be used for multiple transactions. A separate Form 15CA must be filled for each transaction, even if the transactions are related to the same beneficiary.

Is Form 15CB required for all transactions?

The same Form 15CA can be used for multiple transactions, provided that the transactions are of the same nature, i.e., the purpose, amount, and beneficiary are the same for all the transactions.

As per the guidelines issued by the Income Tax Department, a single Form 15CA can be used for multiple transactions if the following conditions are met:

- The nature and purpose of the remittance are the same for all the transactions.
- The amount of remittance is the same for all the transactions.
- The remittance is made to the same beneficiary.
- The country of the remittance is the same for all the transactions.

Who can issue Form 15CB?

Form 15CB is a certificate issued by a Chartered Accountant (CA) in India. The CA certifies that the remittance made by the remitter is not taxable in India and that the tax, if any, has been deducted and deposited with the Indian Government as per the relevant provisions of the Income Tax Act, 1961

What is the validity of Form 15CB?

Form 15CB is valid for six months from the date of its issuance. This means that the remitter should ensure that the remittance is made within six months from the date of issuance of Form 15CB.

Can a foreign company file Form 15CA-15CB?

Yes, a foreign company can file Form 15CA-15CB through its authorized signatory in India.

Is Form 15CA-15CB required for the transfer of funds between NRE and NRO accounts?

No, Form 15CA-15CB is not required to transfer funds between NRE and NRO accounts.

Is Form 15CA-15CB required for remittances to Nepal and Bhutan?

No, Form 15CA-15CB is not required for remittances to Nepal and Bhutan.

Is Form 15CA-15CB required for remittances from India to a person holding a Permanent Account Number (PAN) in India?

No, Form 15CA-15CB is not required for remittances from India to a person holding a Permanent Account Number (PAN) in India.

Form 15CA-15CB is required only for remittances made to non-resident or foreign entities. Since a person holding a PAN in India is considered a resident for tax purposes, Form 15CA-15CB is not applicable in such cases.

Can Form 15CA-15CB be filed after the remittance is made?

Form 15CA and 15CB are required to be filed before making a remittance outside India. However, in certain cases, where the remittance is made without filing Form 15CA/15CB, the remitter can apply to the Assessing Officer (AO) for condonation of delay. If the AO is satisfied with the reasons for not filing the forms, they may allow the remitter to file them after the remittance.

# Income Tax Return (ITR) 3 Form Filing Online in India

The **ITR 3 form** is applicable for individuals and Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs) earning income from **business or profession**. Filing **ITR 3 online in India** ensures tax compliance, accurate disclosure of income, and timely submission on the **income tax e-filing portal** for AY 2026-27.

For end-to-end assistance, explore [income tax filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax-filing) services by IndiaFilings.

## What is ITR 3 Form?

The **ITR 3 form** is an **Income Tax Return** form prescribed by the Income Tax Department of India. It is designed for **individuals and HUFs** who have income from carrying on a **business or profession**. Unlike ITR 1 or ITR 2, ITR 3 covers a broader range of income sources including **capital gains**, foreign income, and partnership firms.

If your income is only from salary or house property, you may consider filing under [ITR 1 Sahaj Form](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-1-sahaj-form) instead.

### Who Should File ITR 3?

- Individuals with **income from business or profession**
- **Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs)** with business income
- Partners in a **[partnership firm](https://www.indiafilings.com/partnership)**
- Individuals with **capital gains income** along with business income
- Freelancers and **self-employed professionals**

### Difference Between ITR 1, ITR 2, and ITR 3

| Form | Applicable For | Business Income | Capital Gains |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ITR 1 | Salaried individuals | No | No |
| [ITR 2](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-2-form) | Individuals & HUFs (no business income) | No | Yes |
| **[ITR 3](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-3-form)** | **Individuals & HUFs (business/profession)** | **Yes** | **Yes** |

## What are the Key Details for ITR-3 AY 2026-27?

For **Assessment Year 2026-27**, the ITR 3 form includes several important updates. The **ITR 3 due date AY 2026-27** for non-audit cases is **31st July 2026**, while for audit cases it is **31st October 2026**. Taxpayers must ensure accurate disclosure of **income from business or profession**, **capital gains**, and foreign assets.

| Category | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Assessment Year | AY 2026-27 (FY 2025-26) |
| Applicable To | Individuals & HUFs with business/profession income |
| Due Date (Non-Audit) | 31st July 2026 |
| Due Date (Audit Cases) | 31st October 2026 |
| Mode of Filing | Online (e-filing) / Offline |
| Verification | e-Verify via Aadhaar OTP, Net Banking, or [DSC](https://www.indiafilings.com/digital-signature) |

## What is the Structure of the ITR-3 Form?

The **ITR 3 form structure** is divided into multiple parts and schedules to capture comprehensive income details. Understanding the **ITR 3 balance sheet** and **profit and loss** requirements is essential for accurate filing.

### Parts and Schedules of ITR 3

| Part/Schedule | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Part A – General | Personal information, filing status, Aadhaar details |
| Part A-BS | Balance Sheet as on 31st March of the financial year |
| Part A-P&L | Profit & Loss Account for the financial year |
| Part A-OI | Other Information – method of accounting, etc. |
| Part A-QD | Quantitative details of trading account |
| Part B-TI | Computation of Total Income |
| Part B-TTI | Computation of Tax Liability on Total Income |
| Schedules (S, HP, BP, CG, OS, etc.) | Detailed schedules for each income head |

### Income Sources Covered Under ITR 3

- **Income from salary** (if any)
- **Income from house property**
- **Business or profession income**
- **Capital gains** (short-term and long-term)
- Income from other sources
- Foreign income and assets

## What are the Changes Made in ITR-3 in 2026?

The Income Tax Department has introduced key revisions in **ITR 3 for AY 2026-27**. These changes aim to improve **income tax compliance** and bring more transparency in **business income tax filing**.

### Key Changes in ITR 3 for AY 2026-27

- New disclosure requirement for **Legal Entity Identifier (LEI)** for refunds above ₹50 crore
- Enhanced reporting of **capital gains** segregated by date of transaction (pre/post 23rd July 2024)
- Mandatory reporting of **buyback of shares** as dividend income
- New columns for **[TDS](https://www.indiafilings.com/tds-return-filing) on salary under Section 192**
- Updated schedule for **foreign assets and income** disclosure
- Revised **deductions under Section 80C to 80U** fields
- Additional reporting for **virtual digital assets (VDA/crypto)** transactions

For businesses needing to file returns, explore [business tax return filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-itr-filing) services for complete compliance support.

## What is the Eligibility Criteria for Filing ITR 3?

Understanding **ITR 3 form eligibility** is crucial before initiating the filing process. The form is specifically applicable to a defined category of taxpayers under the **Income Tax Act, 1961**.

### Who is Eligible to File ITR 3?

- Individuals with **income from business or profession**
- **HUF income tax return** filers with business income
- Individuals who are **partners in a firm** (not carrying business themselves)
- Taxpayers with income from **more than one house property**
- Persons with **foreign assets or foreign income**
- **ITR for freelancers India** – applicable for freelancers under presumptive taxation with audit

### Who Cannot File ITR 3?

- Companies and [LLPs](https://www.indiafilings.com/llp-registration)(they must file [ITR 6](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-6-form) or [ITR 5](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-5-form) respectively)
- Individuals with **only salaried income** (should use ITR 1 or ITR 2)
- Persons opting for **presumptive taxation under Section 44AD/44ADA** without audit (use ITR 4)

If you're a firm or LLP, check out [ITR 5 Form](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-5-form) filing requirements.

## What are the ITR-3 Tax Slabs for AY 2026-27 (FY 2025-26)?

Taxpayers filing **ITR 3 for AY 2026-27** can choose between the
**Old Tax Regime** and the **New Tax Regime (default)**,
with a **4% Health and Education Cess** applicable under both regimes.

### New Tax Regime – Income Tax Slabs for AY 2026-27 (Default)

| Income Slab (₹) | Tax Rate |
| --- | --- |
| Up to ₹3,00,000 | Nil |
| ₹3,00,001 – ₹7,00,000 | 5% |
| ₹7,00,001 – ₹10,00,000 | 10% |
| ₹10,00,001 – ₹12,00,000 | 15% |
| ₹12,00,001 – ₹15,00,000 | 20% |
| Above ₹15,00,000 | 30% |

### Old Tax Regime – Income Tax Slabs for AY 2026-27

| Income Slab (₹) | Tax Rate – Below 60 Years | Tax Rate – Senior Citizens (60–80 Years) | Tax Rate – Super Senior Citizens (80+ Years) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Up to ₹2,50,000 | Nil | Nil | Nil |
| ₹2,50,001 – ₹3,00,000 | 5% | Nil | Nil |
| ₹3,00,001 – ₹5,00,000 | 5% | 5% | Nil |
| ₹5,00,001 – ₹10,00,000 | 20% | 20% | 20% |
| Above ₹10,00,000 | 30% | 30% | 30% |

## What are the Restrictions to Using an ITR Form 3 for Filing an ITR?

While **ITR 3** covers a wide range of income sources, there are specific restrictions that taxpayers must be aware of to avoid filing the wrong form.

### Key Restrictions for ITR 3 Filing

- Cannot be used by **companies, firms, LLPs, or trusts**
- Not applicable for individuals with **only presumptive income under Section 44AD, 44ADA, or 44AE** without audit (must use [ITR 4 Sugam Form](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-4-sugam-form))
- Cannot be filed if total income is below the **basic exemption limit** and there is no other mandatory filing requirement
- Not for assessees required to file under **Section 139(4A), (4B), (4C), or (4D)** – they must use [ITR 7 Form](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-7-form)
- Cannot include income of **minor children clubbed** under certain special scenarios

## What Documents are Required for ITR 3 Form Filing?

Having all necessary documents ready ensures a smooth **ITR 3 online submission** process. Below is a comprehensive list of documents required for **ITR 3 filing for AY 2026-27**.

### Financial Documents Needed

- [PAN card](https://www.indiafilings.com/pan-card) and [Aadhaar card](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/eaadhaar-download)

### Business & Profession Related Documents

- **Profit & Loss Account** and Balance Sheet
- Books of accounts (if applicable)
- **Tax audit report** under Section 44AB (if applicable)
- GST returns and TDS certificates
- Details of **capital gains** transactions (sale deeds, stock statements)
- Foreign asset and income details (if applicable)

## What is the Old vs New Tax Regime for ITR-3?

Taxpayers filing **ITR 3 for AY 2026-27** must choose between the **old tax regime** and the **ITR 3 new tax regime**. The choice significantly impacts the **tax liability and available deductions**.

### Comparison: Old vs New Tax Regime

| Feature | Old Tax Regime | New Tax Regime (Default) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tax Slabs | 5%, 20%, 30% | 0%, 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 30% |
| Standard Deduction | ₹50,000 | ₹75,000 |
| Section 80C Deduction | Available (up to ₹1.5 lakh) | Not Available |

## What are the Deadlines and Due Dates for ITR 3 Filing AY 2026-27?

Missing the **ITR filing last date 2026-27** can attract penalties and interest under the Income Tax Act. It is crucial to be aware of all **ITR 3 due dates** for timely compliance.

| Individuals/HUFs (Non-Audit) | 31st July 2026 |
| Audit Cases (Business/Profession) | 31st October 2026 |

### Consequences of Late Filing

- **Late fee of ₹5,000** under Section 234F (₹1,000 if income is below ₹5 lakh)
- **Interest under Section 234A** at 1% per month on unpaid tax
- Loss of ability to **carry forward losses** from business or capital gains
- Possible scrutiny and **income tax notice** from the department

If you have filed incorrectly, you can still rectify it through a [revised return](https://www.indiafilings.com/revised-return) before the due date.

## Frequently asked questions

Common questions aboutITR-3 Form.

What is the ITR 3 form?

The ITR-3 form is an income tax return form used in India for individuals and Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs) who earn income from a business or profession.

Who should file the ITR-3 form?

Individuals or HUFs should file the ITR-3 form if they meet specific criteria, including being a company director, receiving pension income, earning income from house property, or having investments in unlisted equity shares.

Who is not eligible to file the ITR-3 form?

Individuals or HUFs earning income as a partner of a partnership firm engaged in a business or profession fall out of ITR 3 applicability. They should file the ITR-2 form instead of the ITR-3.

What is ITR 3 due date for filing it for non-audit cases in the assessment year 2023-24?

The due date for non-audit cases for the assessment year 2023-24 is July 31, 2023.

What are the penalties for late filing of the ITR-3 form in India?

If filed after the due date but before December 31 of the assessment year, a late filing fee of 5,000 may be levied. If filed after December 31, a late filing fee of 10,000 may be levied. The fee may vary based on income and other factors.

What documents are required to file the ITR-3 form?

Required documents include PAN, Aadhaar card, bank account details, Form 16 (if applicable), investment details, and books of accounts (for business or professional income).

How many sections are there in the ITR-3 form?

The ITR-3 form is divided into six sections: General Information, Income Details, Deductions and Taxes Paid, TDS/TCS Credit, Verification and Declaration, and Schedules.

What information is required in the "Income Details" section of the ITR-3 form?

This section requires disclosure of income from various sources, including salaries, pensions, annuities, family pensions, and other avenues, along with total taxable income and tax liability calculation.

Can I claim deductions in the ITR-3 form?

Yes, you can claim deductions permitted under various sections of the Income Tax Act in the "Deductions and Taxes Paid" section.

What is TDS and TCS credit in the ITR-3 form?

TDS stands for Tax Deducted at Source, and TCS stands for Tax Collected at Source. You need to include details of these credits in the respective section.

How can I verify my ITR-3 form?

You can verify your ITR-3 form either through a digital signature or by sending a physical copy of the signed return to the Centralized Processing Center (CPC).

Why should I choose IndiaFilings for filing the ITR-3 form?

IndiaFilings offers expert guidance, accurate filing, documentation assistance, secure filing, and timely reminders to simplify the ITR-3 filing process.

Is there a specific format to fill out the ITR-3 form?

Yes, the ITR-3 form must be filled out following the format and guidelines provided by the Income Tax Department.

Are there any exceptions to the late filing penalties for the ITR-3 form?

If your total income is less than 5 lakh, the maximum late filing fee is capped at 1,000.

What should I do if I miss the due date for filing the ITR-3 form?

If you miss the due date, you should file your ITR-3 form as soon as possible to avoid additional late filing penalties and potential legal consequences.

# Chartered Accountant Certificate Online in India

A **chartered accountant certificate online in India** is an official document issued by a practising Chartered Accountant that validates specific financial information about an individual or business. Whether you need proof of income, net worth, or foreign remittance, a **CA signed certificate India** serves as a credible financial document recognised by banks, embassies, and government authorities across the country. [Learn what a CA certificate is and why you need it.](https://www.indiafilings.com/ca-certificates/what-is-a-ca-certificate-and-why-do-we-need-it)

## What is a Chartered Accountant Certificate and Why Does India Require It?

A **CA attestation certificate** is a formal declaration by a licensed CA that certifies the accuracy of financial statements or documents. In India, these certificates are mandatory for numerous legal, financial, and administrative processes.

Businesses, individuals, NRIs, and students frequently require **CA certificate for income proof** or **CA certificate for bank loan** purposes. The document carries the CA's seal, signature, and membership number, making it legally valid across institutions.

- Required for visa applications, loan processing, and scholarship grants
- Mandatory for FEMA compliance and foreign remittance transactions
- Used for turnover certification during government tenders
- Essential for property purchase and employment verification

### Types of CA Certificates in India

| Certificate Type | Purpose | Issued For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Net Worth Certificate | Visa, Loan, Property | Individuals & Businesses |
| Income Proof Certificate | Bank Loan, Scholarship | Salaried & Self-employed |
| Foreign Remittance Certificate | FEMA Compliance | NRIs & Businesses |
| Turnover Certificate | Government Tenders | Businesses |
| Funds Certificate | Visa, Education | Students & Individuals |

## How Does a CA Certificate for Net Worth Help Indian Businesses and Individuals?

The [**CA certificate for net worth**](https://www.indiafilings.com/ca-certificates/ca-certificate-for-net-worth) is one of the most widely requested certificates in India. It provides a verified summary of an individual's or company's total assets minus liabilities, offering a transparent picture of financial health to concerned authorities.

Banks, embassies, and government agencies rely on this **online CA certificate service** to evaluate financial eligibility. A net worth certificate is particularly critical during property transactions, business registrations, and immigration processes.

- Validates financial standing for visa and immigration purposes
- Required during business loan applications and credit evaluations
- Used to establish credibility in high-value property dealings
- Helps businesses qualify for government contracts and tenders

## Why Should You Apply for a CA Certificate Online in India for Visa Purposes?

Embassies and consulates across the world require a **CA certificate for visa application** as proof of sufficient financial resources. The **CA certificate application online** process in India has simplified this significantly, allowing applicants to obtain verified documents without visiting a CA's office in person.

Whether you are applying for a student visa, tourist visa, or work permit, a **CA certificate for funds** confirms that you have adequate financial backing to sustain yourself abroad. IndiaFilings connects you with experienced CAs who issue **CA certificate for foreign remittance** and visa-related certificates promptly.

- Accepted by consulates of the USA, UK, Canada, Australia, and more
- Covers funds, income, and net worth as required by visa authorities
- Issued with digital signatures for faster processing
- Valid for scholarship and education visa applications as well

### Key Benefits of Applying for a CA Certificate Online

- Save time with doorstep document collection and online submission
- Get certified by ICAI-registered CAs with verified credentials
- Receive your **CA certificate format India** compliant document quickly
- Secure handling of sensitive financial data with complete confidentiality

## How Does CA Certificate for GST Compliance Support Indian Businesses?

Businesses registered under the [**GST return filing**](https://www.indiafilings.com/gst-return-filing) framework often need a **CA certificate for GST compliance** during audits, assessments, or legal proceedings. This certificate affirms that a business has correctly declared its turnover and complied with applicable GST regulations.

A **CA certificate for audit** or compliance is also frequently demanded during departmental scrutiny or when applying for government licences. IndiaFilings simplifies this process by connecting businesses with CAs who specialise in GST and tax compliance certifications.

- Confirms accurate GST filing and turnover declaration
- Required during GST audits and annual return filings
- Supports businesses in resolving tax disputes with authorities
- Needed for export-oriented units claiming GST refunds

## What is the Role of a CA Certificate Under FEMA for NRIs in India?

Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) dealing with property, investments, or fund transfers in India require a **CA certificate under FEMA** to comply with the Foreign Exchange Management Act. This certificate certifies that the funds being transferred or invested are from legitimate sources and comply with Indian regulations.

The **CA certificate for NRI** is especially important for repatriation of sale proceeds from property transactions in India. You can also get a **CA certificate for import export** to facilitate international trade transactions under FEMA guidelines. Filing your [**income tax**](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax-filing) correctly is a prerequisite for obtaining many of these certificates.

- Mandatory for repatriation of NRI property sale proceeds
- Required for inward and outward foreign remittance compliance
- Supports NRI investment declarations in Indian markets
- Used in import-export transactions for regulatory compliance

## How to Get a Chartered Accountant Certificate Online in India?

Obtaining a **chartered accountant certificate online in India** through IndiaFilings is a straightforward process. The platform connects you with ICAI-registered CAs who assess your documents and issue the required certificate efficiently.

Follow these steps to apply for your **CA certificate online India**:

1. **Select the Certificate Type:** Choose the specific [**CA certificate format**](https://www.indiafilings.com/ca-certificates/understanding-the-ca-certificate-format) you need — net worth, income proof, funds, turnover, or FEMA compliance.
2. **Submit Your Documents:** Upload relevant financial documents such as bank statements, ITR filings, balance sheets, or property papers.
3. **CA Review & Verification:** A qualified CA will review, verify, and validate your submitted financial information thoroughly.
4. **Certificate Issuance:** Your signed and sealed **CA certificate for bank loan**, visa, or other purpose is issued and delivered digitally.

# ITR 5 Form Filing Online in India – AY 2026-27

The **ITR 5 form** is applicable for partnership firms, LLPs, Association of Persons (AOPs), Body of Individuals (BOIs), and co-operative societies. Filing **ITR 5 online** ensures accurate **[income tax compliance](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax-filing)** for non-individual entities in India for AY 2026-27.

What is ITR 5 Form?

The **ITR 5 form** is an **Income Tax Return** form prescribed by the Income Tax Department of India. It is specifically designed for entities other than individuals, HUFs, and companies. The form covers a wide range of non-individual entities including **[partnership firms](https://www.indiafilings.com/partnership)**, **[Limited Liability Partnerships](https://www.indiafilings.com/llp-registration)(LLPs)**, **Association of Persons (AOPs)**, **Body of Individuals (BOIs)**, co-operative societies, and artificial juridical persons. The ITR 5 form enables these entities to declare their income, claim deductions, and compute their tax liability in compliance with the Income Tax Act, 1961.

### Who Should File ITR 5 Form?

- **Partnership firms** registered under the Indian Partnership Act
- **Limited Liability Partnerships (LLPs)** registered under the LLP Act, 2008
- **Association of Persons (AOPs)** and **Body of Individuals (BOIs)**
- **Co-operative societies** and local authorities
- **Artificial juridical persons** not covered under other ITR forms
- Entities with **income from business or profession**
- Firms with **capital gains** or foreign income

### Difference Between ITR 5 and Other ITR Forms

| Form | Applicable For | Business Income | Capital Gains |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ITR 3 | Individuals and HUFs with business income | Yes | Yes |
| ITR 4 | Individuals, HUFs, Firms (presumptive taxation) | Yes (Presumptive) | No |
| **ITR 5** | **Partnership Firms, LLPs, AOPs, BOIs** | **Yes** | **Yes** |
| ITR 6 | Companies (other than Section 11 exemption) | Yes | Yes |
| ITR 7 | [Trusts](https://www.indiafilings.com/trust-registration), political parties, [charitable institutions](https://www.indiafilings.com/producer-company-registration) | Limited | Yes |

## What are the Key Details of ITR 5 for AY 2026-27?

For **Assessment Year 2026-27**, the **ITR 5 form** has been updated with new disclosure requirements and revised schedules. Entities must ensure accurate reporting of **firm income tax filing** details and timely submission on the **[income tax](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax) e-filing portal**. Entities with **business turnover** and professional income can explore complete [business tax return filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/business-itr-filing) support for hassle-free compliance.

| Category | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Assessment Year | AY 2026-27 (FY 2025-26) |
| Applicable To | Partnership Firms, LLPs, AOPs, BOIs, Co-operative Societies |
| Due Date (Non-Audit) | 31st July 2026 |
| Due Date (Audit Cases) | 31st October 2026 |
| Mode of Filing | Online (e-filing) – Mandatory for most entities |
| Verification | [Digital Signature Certificate](https://www.indiafilings.com/digital-signature) (DSC) – Mandatory for audit cases |
| Tax Rate for Firms and LLPs | 30% flat rate plus applicable surcharge and cess |

## What is the Structure of ITR 5 Form?

The **ITR 5 form structure** is comprehensive and covers multiple parts and schedules to capture detailed income and financial information of non-individual entities. Understanding the form structure is essential for accurate **[ITR 5 online submission](https://www.indiafilings.com/learn/itr-5-filing)**.

### Parts and Schedules of ITR 5

| Part or Schedule | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Part A – General | Entity information, nature of business, registration details |
| Part A-BS | Balance Sheet as on 31st March of the financial year |
| Part A-P and L | Profit and Loss Account for the financial year |
| Part A-OI | Other Information – method of accounting, inventory valuation |
| Part B-TI | Computation of Total Income |
| Part B-TTI | Computation of Tax Liability on Total Income |
| Schedule HP | Income from House Property |
| Schedule BP | Income from Business or Profession |
| Schedule CG | Income from Capital Gains |
| Schedule OS | Income from Other Sources |
| Schedule [TDS](https://www.indiafilings.com/tds-return-filing) and TCS | Details of TDS and TCS deducted and collected |
| Schedule FA | Details of Foreign Assets and Income |

### Income Sources Covered Under ITR 5

- **Income from business or profession**
- **Income from house property**
- **Capital gains** – short-term and long-term
- Income from other sources
- **Foreign income and foreign assets**
- Income from **co-operative societies**
- Income of **local authorities**

## What are the Changes Made in ITR 5 for AY 2026-27?

The Income Tax Department has introduced important revisions in **ITR 5 for AY 2026-27**. These updates aim to improve transparency in **LLP tax filing India** and **AOP tax return filing** and ensure better compliance tracking.

### New Updates in ITR 5 AY 2026-27

- New disclosure requirement for **Legal Entity Identifier (LEI)** for refunds above Rs. 50 crore
- Enhanced reporting of **capital gains** segregated by transaction date before and after 23rd July 2024
- Mandatory reporting of **buyback of shares** as dividend income
- New columns for **TDS on payments under Section 194** series
- Updated schedule for **foreign assets and foreign income** disclosure
- Revised fields for **deductions under Section 80G, 80IA, 80IB**
- New reporting requirement for **virtual digital assets (VDA/crypto)** transactions
- Enhanced **partner details disclosure** including profit sharing ratio

## What is the Eligibility Criteria for Filing ITR 5?

Understanding the **ITR 5 eligibility criteria** is crucial before initiating the filing process. Entities that are not eligible to file ITR 5 must choose the correct form such as [ITR 6 Form](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-6-form) for companies or other applicable forms.

### Who is Eligible to File ITR 5?

- **Partnership firms** registered under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932
- **Limited Liability Partnerships (LLPs)** registered under the LLP Act, 2008
- **Association of Persons (AOPs)** including societies and clubs
- **Body of Individuals (BOIs)**
- **Co-operative societies** registered under the Co-operative Societies Act
- **Local authorities** as defined under the Income Tax Act
- **Artificial juridical persons** not covered under other forms
- Entities with **income from business, profession, capital gains, or other sources**

### Who Cannot File ITR 5?

- Individuals and HUFs who must use [ITR 3 Form](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-3-form) or [ITR 4 Sugam Form](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-4-sugam-form)
- Companies registered under the Companies Act (must use ITR 6)
- Trusts, political parties, and charitable institutions (must use ITR 7)
- Entities required to file under **Section 139(4A), 4B, 4C, or 4D**

## What are the Restrictions to Using ITR 5 Form?

While **ITR 5** covers a wide range of non-individual entities, there are specific restrictions that must be noted. Trusts, charitable institutions, and political parties required to file under Section 139(4A), (4B), or (4C) must use [ITR 7 Form](https://www.indiafilings.com/itr-7-form) and cannot file using ITR 5.

### Key Restrictions for ITR 5 Filing

- Cannot be used by **individuals, HUFs, or companies**
- Not applicable for **trusts or charitable institutions** exempt under Section 11
- Cannot be used by entities required to file under **Section 139(4A), (4B), (4C), or (4D)**
- Entities with **only agricultural income** as the source may not need to file
- Not applicable for entities with **income below the basic exemption limit** without any mandatory filing requirement
- Firms opting for **presumptive taxation under Section 44AD** with turnover below threshold may use **ITR 4 Sugam** instead

## What Documents are Required for ITR 5 Form Filing?

Having the right documents ready ensures a smooth **ITR 5 filing process**. Entities must also ensure their [TDS return filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/tds-return-filing) is up to date before proceeding with the income tax return to avoid discrepancies in Form 26AS.

### Basic KYC and Financial Documents

- [PAN card](https://www.indiafilings.com/pan-card) of the firm, LLP, or entity
- Partnership deed or LLP agreement
- Form 26AS and Annual Information Statement
- Bank account statements for FY 2025-26
- Interest certificates from banks
- Details of all **partners or members** with their PAN and profit sharing ratio

### Business and Entity Related Documents

- **Profit and Loss Account** and Balance Sheet for FY 2025-26
- Books of accounts and supporting vouchers
- **Tax audit report** under Section 44AB if applicable
- GST returns and reconciliation statements
- TDS certificates – Form 16A from clients and deductors
- Details of **capital gains transactions** including sale deeds and stock statements
- Foreign asset and **foreign income details** if applicable
- Details of **advance tax payments** made during the year

## How to File ITR 5 Form Online on Income Tax Portal?

The **ITR 5 online filing process** is mandatory for most entities and must be done through the official **income tax e-filing portal**. Audit cases must mandatorily use a **Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)** for e-verification. In case an [income tax notice](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax-notice) is received during or after the filing process, it must be addressed promptly to avoid penalties.

### Step-by-Step Guide to File ITR 5 Online

01. Log in to **incometax.gov.in** using the entity PAN and registered password
02. Go to e-File, then Income Tax Returns, then File Income Tax Return
03. Select **Assessment Year 2026-27** and filing mode as Online
04. Choose **ITR 5** as the applicable form
05. Select the reason for filing – taxable income exceeds basic exemption limit or mandatory filing
06. Fill in the entity details, partner information, and nature of business
07. Enter **business income details** in Schedule BP
08. Add **capital gains details** in Schedule CG if applicable
09. Fill in **Balance Sheet and Profit and Loss** details in Part A-BS and Part A-P and L
10. Enter **TDS and advance tax payment** details
11. Review the **tax computation** and pay any outstanding tax liability
12. Preview and submit the return
13. e-Verify using **Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)** – mandatory for audit cases

### How to File ITR 5 Using Offline Utility?

Entities can also file **ITR 5 using the offline utility** by downloading the **Excel or Java utility** from the income tax portal, filling in the required details, generating the XML file, and uploading it on the portal. Physical submission is not permitted for ITR 5. The offline utility is ideal for entities with complex financial data that requires careful review before submission.

## What are the Due Dates and Penalties for ITR 5 Filing AY 2026-27?

Missing the **ITR 5 due date** can attract significant penalties and interest. Entities must be aware of all **ITR 5 filing deadlines** for AY 2026-27. Entities that have filed incorrectly can file a [revised return](https://www.indiafilings.com/revised-return) before the deadline to correct any errors. For entities with foreign remittances, compliance with [15CA 15CB filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/15ca-15cb-filing) requirements is also mandatory alongside the income tax return.

### ITR 5 Due Dates AY 2026-27

| Category of Entity | Due Date |
| --- | --- |
| Firms and LLPs (Non-Audit) | 31st July 2026 |
| Audit Cases (Firms, LLPs, AOPs, BOIs) | 31st October 2026 |
| Transfer Pricing Cases | 30th November 2026 |
| Belated Return | 31st December 2026 |
| Revised Return | 31st December 2026 |

### Penalty for Late Filing of ITR 5

- Late fee of **Rs. 5,000** under Section 234F (Rs. 1,000 if total income is below Rs. 5 lakh)
- Interest under **Section 234A** at 1% per month on unpaid tax liability
- Loss of ability to **carry forward business losses and capital losses**
- Possible scrutiny and **income tax notice** from the department
- Penalty under **Section 271F** for non-filing in certain cases

IndiaFilings is a trusted platform for **ITR 5 form filing online in India**, offering expert-assisted services for partnership firms, LLPs, AOPs, and co-operative societies. Our qualified tax professionals ensure accurate and timely **income tax return for partnership firms** and **LLP annual filing**, handling everything from document preparation to DSC-based e-verification for AY 2026-27.

## Frequently asked questions

Common questions aboutITR-5 Form.

Who should file the ITR-5 Form?

The ITR-5 Form is meant for firms, Limited Liability Partnerships (LLPs), Bodies of Individuals (BOIs), Associations of Persons (AOPs), estates of deceased individuals, artificial juridical persons, business trusts, investment funds, insolvent individuals, estates, cooperative societies, and local authorities. However, individuals falling under specific sections like 139(4A), 139(4C), 139(4B), or 139(4D) should not use this form.

What is the due date for filing the ITR-5 Form?

The due date for filing ITR-5 depends on whether the taxpayers accounts need to be audited or whether they must furnish a report in Form No. 3CEB. Its 31st October for audited accounts, 30th November if Form No. 3CEB is required, and 31st July for other cases.

Who cannot use the ITR-5 Form?

The ITR-5 Form is not suitable for individual assesses, Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs), companies (except those claiming exemption under section 11), and taxpayers falling under Sections 139(4A), 139(4B), 139(4C), 139(4D), 139(4E), or 139(4F), who are required to use Form ITR-7.

Are any documents required to be attached to the ITR-5 form

No, there is no requirement to attach documents with the ITR-5 form.

What is the structure of the ITR-5 Form?

The ITR-5 Form comprises several parts and schedules, including sections for general information, balance sheets, manufacturing accounts, trading accounts, profit and loss accounts, quantitative details, computation of total income, tax liability, and schedules for various income sources.

What the recommended sequence for filling out the ITR-5 Form?

The Income Tax Department recommends the following sequence: Part A, Schedules, Part B, and Verification.

Why choose IndiaFilings for ITR-5 filing?

IndiaFilings offers expert guidance, deduction optimization, review and verification services, secure filing, timely reminders for tax deadlines, and post-filing support, making the ITR-5 filing process easy, accurate, and hassle-free.

Can a local authority use the ITR-5 Form for filing taxes?

Yes, local authorities can use the ITR-5 Form for filing their income tax returns.

What if my accounts need to be audited, and I miss the due date for filing ITR-5?

Missing the due date for filing ITR-5 when accounts need to be audited can lead to penalties and consequences as per the Income-Tax Act.

Is it mandatory to e-file the ITR-5 Form?

Yes, for certain taxpayers, e-filing of the ITR-5 Form is mandatory as per income tax regulations.

Can an LLP (Limited Liability Partnership) file the ITR-5 Form?

Yes, an LLP can use the ITR-5 Form for filing income tax returns.

Is there any special schedule for reporting foreign income in the ITR-5 Form?

Yes, Schedule FSI is used to report income from outside India and tax relief.

Can a business trust or investment fund use the ITR-5 Form?

Yes, business trusts and investment funds are among the entities eligible to use the ITR-5 Form.

What is the penalty for late filing of the ITR-5 Form?

The penalty for late filing varies depending on the extent of delay and the taxpayers income. Its essential to file on time to avoid penalties.

Can the ITR-5 Form be revised after filing?

Yes, you can revise the ITR-5 Form within the specified time limit if you discover any errors or omissions after the initial filing.

Are there any income tax deductions specifically available for entities using the ITR-5 Form?

The ITR-5 Form allows entities to claim deductions under various sections of the Income Tax Act, depending on their eligibility and sources of income.

What is the role of Form No. 3CEB in determining the due date for filing ITR-5?

If a taxpayer is required to furnish a report in Form No. 3CEB, the due date for filing ITR-5 is extended to 30th November.

Can an estate of a deceased individual use the ITR-5 Form?

Yes, estates of deceased individuals can use the ITR-5 Form for filing income tax returns.

Is there a fee for filing the ITR-5 Form through IndiaFilings?

IndiaFilings may charge a fee for its services, and the fee may vary depending on the specific service package chosen by the taxpayer. We offer services at competitive and affordable prices to assist taxpayers with their ITR-5 filing needs.

What if I make a mistake in the ITR-5 Form after filing it?

If you discover an error or omission in the ITR-5 Form after filing, you can rectify it by filing a revised return within the specified time limit.

## What is ITR-7 Return Filing Online in India?

ITR-7 is a specialized tax return form filed by non-individual entities in India such as trusts, NGOs, societies, and charitable organizations that earn income from various sources. This form requires detailed disclosure of income, deductions, and financial position as mandated by the Income Tax Act. ITR-7 return filing online ensures these entities maintain transparency and comply with tax regulations.

- NGOs and charitable organizations
- [Trusts registered](https://www.indiafilings.com/trust-registration) with charitable status
- Societies with taxable income
- Non-profit organizations
- Entities registered under section 12A of the [Income Tax Act](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax)

## What is the Purpose of the ITR-7 Form in India?

The purpose of ITR-7 form in India is to provide a structured framework for non-individual charitable entities to report their annual income, expenses, and financial position to the tax department. ITR-7 ensures transparency in operations of NGOs, trusts, and charitable organizations while allowing them to claim exemptions and deductions they are entitled to. Filing ITR-7 online helps these entities demonstrate accountability to donors, government, and the general public.

### **Core Objectives of ITR-7 Filing in India**

- Reporting charitable income and activities
- Claiming tax exemptions and deductions
- Maintaining financial transparency
- Demonstrating compliance with tax laws

Any NGO, trust, society, or charitable organization in India that has taxable income exceeding the exemption limit must file ITR-7 online within the prescribed due date. Even organizations with tax-exempt status may need to file ITR-7 to report exempt income and claim deductions. Filing ITR-7 online is mandatory for maintaining charitable registration and avoiding penalties.

### **Eligibility Criteria for ITR-7 Filing in India**

- A registered society with taxable income
- A charitable organization with income exceeding exemption threshold
- An entity with Section 12A exemption status requiring [12A registration](https://www.indiafilings.com/12a-registration)

## What is the Format of the ITR-7 Return in India?

The ITR-7 return format in India is structured with multiple schedules designed to capture comprehensive financial information about charitable activities and income sources. The format requires entities to report both exempt income and taxable income separately, providing clear visibility of financial operations. Understanding ITR-7 format helps organizations fill the form accurately and avoid rejection or tax department queries.

### **Components of ITR-7 Format in India**

- Part A: Identification and entity details
- Part B: Income computation and schedules
- Supporting schedules for income sources
- Balance sheet and financial position
- Exemption and deduction claims
- Tax computation and liability

## What are the Different Sections of the ITR-7 Form in India?

The ITR-7 form in India is organized into distinct sections, each capturing specific aspects of an organization's financial activities and tax position. Each section requires detailed information relevant to charitable operations and income reporting. Proper completion of all sections ensures comprehensive disclosure and reduces chances of tax department scrutiny.

### **Key Sections of ITR-7 Form in India**

- **Schedule 1:** Entity identification and registration details
- **Schedule 2:** Income computation from various sources
- **Schedule 3:** Details of exempted income
- **Schedule 4:** Deductions and exemptions claimed

- **Schedule 7:** Specific transaction details

## Which Documents Are Required for ITR-7 Return Filing Online in India?

To file ITR-7 return online in India, you need comprehensive documentation that supports your income declarations, deductions claimed, and charitable status. Having all required documents ready streamlines the ITR-7 filing process and reduces errors. Keep digital copies of all documents for quick reference during online filing and [income tax filing](https://www.indiafilings.com/income-tax-filing) requirements.

## How Can You File ITR-7 Online Step by Step in India?

Filing ITR-7 online in India involves several systematic steps through the e-filing portal managed by the Income Tax Department. The ITR-7 online filing process is secure and allows organizations to track their filing status in real-time. Following this step-by-step approach ensures error-free submission of your ITR-7 return.

The ITR-7 filing due date for AY 2026-27 in India is July 31st of the following financial year for most organizations, though certain categories may have extended deadlines. Audit requirements for NGOs filing ITR-7 in India depend on the organization's turnover and nature of activities. Late filing of ITR-7 in India attracts penalties under section 271F of the Income Tax Act, which increases financial burden on NGOs and charitable organizations. The penalty amount varies based on the delay period and circumstances of late filing. Understanding ITR-7 penalties motivates timely filing and maintains your organization's tax compliance status.

## What is a Legal Notice and How Does It Work in India?

A legal notice is a formal written communication sent to an individual or entity, informing them of your intention to take legal action if the matter is not resolved. It serves as the first step in dispute resolution and is recognised under the **Code of Civil Procedure (CPC)** in India.

When you send a **legal notice in India**, you officially put the other party on record that a grievance exists. It gives them an opportunity to resolve the matter before escalating to court, saving both time and legal costs.

- Acts as a formal warning before filing a lawsuit
- Establishes a legal record of the dispute
- Gives the opposing party a chance to settle
- Recognised and enforceable under Indian law
- Can be sent via registered post, courier, or email

## Why Should You Send a Legal Notice Online for Disputes in India?

The traditional process of drafting and sending a legal notice involved multiple visits to a lawyer's office and significant delays. With **online legal notice drafting services in India**, you can get a professionally drafted notice quickly and conveniently from anywhere.

## What are the Types of Legal Notices You Can Send in India?

Legal notices in India cover a wide range of disputes. Understanding which type of notice applies to your situation is critical for taking the right legal step. Here is an overview of the most common types of **legal notices sent online in India**.

### Legal Notice for Money Recovery

A **legal notice for money recovery** is sent when a person or business owes you money and refuses to pay. This is one of the most common types of legal notices issued in India and is an essential precursor to filing a civil suit for recovery of dues. Learn more about [legal notice for non-payment of dues](https://www.indiafilings.com/legal-notice/legal-notice-for-non-payment-of-dues).

### Legal Notice for Cheque Bounce

Under **Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act**, a **legal notice for cheque bounce** must be sent within 30 days of receiving the cheque dishonour memo. Failure to send the notice within this period can affect your legal standing in court.

### Legal Notice for Property Dispute

Property-related conflicts, such as illegal occupation, ownership disputes, or tenant issues, require a formal **legal notice for property dispute in India**. This notice sets out your claims and demands action from the other party within a specified timeframe.

### Legal Notice for Breach of Contract

When a party fails to fulfil their contractual obligations, a **legal notice for breach of contract in India** formally communicates the violation and demands either performance or compensation.

## How Do You Draft a Legal Notice Online in India?

Drafting a **legal notice** requires precise language, accurate facts, and knowledge of applicable laws. An incorrectly drafted notice can weaken your case or even be dismissed. Here are the essential steps to draft a legal notice online in India:

1. **Identify the dispute:** Clearly define the nature of your grievance — money recovery, cheque bounce, property, or contract breach.
2. **Gather documents:** Collect all relevant agreements, invoices, communications, and supporting evidence. Check the [documents required for legal notices](https://www.indiafilings.com/legal-notice/documents-required-for-legal-notices) for a complete list.

4. **Draft the notice:** The notice must include the sender's details, recipient's details, facts of the dispute, legal provisions, and the relief sought.
5. **Review and approve:** Review the draft carefully before finalising it.
6. **Send via registered post or email:** Sending via registered post creates an official record. **Legal notice via email** is also accepted in certain circumstances.

Understanding the **legal notice procedure in India** can significantly impact the outcome of your dispute. Sending a notice not only asserts your legal rights but also demonstrates your intent to resolve the matter lawfully.

A well-drafted notice using the correct **legal notice format India** can strengthen your position in court if the matter escalates. Courts often view the issuance of a prior notice as a sign of good faith and procedural compliance.
